title: Stop showing raw e.toString() as the device-restore error message in RestoreStatus/DeviceRestoreService
rule: EH-5 / AX-2 (no pre-formatted human messages; ARB-only user text)
why: RestoreStatus.error(message: String) is a raw String, not a code/enum, and DeviceRestoreService feeds it e.toString() directly — a raw exception message (e.g. 'Exception: Data pull failed: [firebase_firestore/unavailable] ...'). device_restore_screen.dart renders this string verbatim next to a properly-localized l10n.deviceRestoreFailed headline (lines 214-222), so any restore failure — plausible on flaky mobile networks, which this cloud-restore flow specifically targets — shows raw, untranslated, technical English text to Hebrew-locale users today, live, with no masking guard. Separately, RestoreStatus.restoring's `phase` field is a hardcoded English sentence matched by string equality in _localizePhase(); the two files' string literals must stay in lockstep by convention only — if either drifts, the fallback silently renders the raw English phase instead of erroring.
recommendation: Replace RestoreStatus.error's free-text `message` with a stable error code/enum resolved via AppLocalizations in the screen (mirroring how `phase` already works, but with a sealed type instead of string matching so drift is a compile error).
acceptance_criteria: RestoreStatus.error carries a typed code (enum or sealed subtype), not a raw String built from e.toString().
A Locale('he') widget test pumps a forced restore failure and asserts the rendered error text is 100% ARB-sourced (no raw exception text).
phase and the error code share one sealed type/enum between DeviceRestoreService and the screen so an unmapped case fails to compile instead of silently falling back to English.

title: Fix app_shell.dart's fixed-height context banners — they truncate text under accessibility scaling and undersize the exit-button tap targets
rule: AX-4 (no fixed heights on text wrappers; 48dp targets)
why: _ChildViewBanner (height: 28), TutorModeIndicatorBar (height: 24), and ProfileSwitcherBar (height: 44) are hardcoded-height Containers wrapping Text with maxLines:1/overflow:ellipsis and fontSize 11-14; none of them scale with MediaQuery.textScaler. At a larger accessibility text-scale setting, a real, present-day user segment sees the child/talmid name or role badge clipped tighter than intended, or the row overflowing the fixed bar. Independent of text scale, the Exit buttons in the first two banners are geometrically provable to be under the 48dp minimum: an icon(12)+padding(vertical:2x2)+text(11sp) inside a 24-28dp-tall parent caps the whole tap target at roughly 20-24dp — well short of 48dp — for a control (exiting parent/tutor mode) that a stressed or motor-impaired user needs to hit reliably.
recommendation: Let the banner Containers size to content (IntrinsicHeight or padding-driven, not a literal height:), and grow the Exit InkWell's hit area to kMinInteractiveDimension via padding/ConstrainedBox independent of the visual bar height.
acceptance_criteria: _ChildViewBanner, TutorModeIndicatorBar, and ProfileSwitcherBar no longer hardcode a literal `height:` that can clip scaled text.
A widget test pumped at TextScaler.linear(1.3)+ and Locale('he') asserts no RenderFlex overflow and no truncated semantics label on these three banners.
The Exit/tap affordance in each banner measures >=48dp in its tappable dimension (verified via a hitTestable finder or explicit SizedBox/ConstrainedBox in the widget tree).

corrections: The '20-24dp' tap-target estimate is slightly generous; closer computation gives ~18-20dp for the _ChildViewBanner/TutorModeIndicatorBar Exit buttons — still well short of 48dp, so the conclusion is unaffected.

title: Constrain AnalyticsService.logEvent to the AnalyticsEvent catalog — LogEvents-sourced calls leak profile_id and content identifiers to Firebase Analytics

evidence.quote: // Typed string constants for structured log event names.

why: AnalyticsService.logEvent(String name, ...) accepts any bare string, so nothing stops a caller from importing LogEvents — documented in its own header as 'structured log event names' for AppLogger, not an analytics catalog — and piping it straight into real Firebase Analytics. Grepping every `.logEvent(` call site in lib/ shows ~15 places do exactly this, bypassing the audited 12-event AnalyticsEvent catalog and its PV-1 review entirely. At least 7 of those sites attach identifying data: outbox_processor.dart fires sync_outbox_dead_lettered with entity_key = '${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}' (confirmed composition in completion_writer.dart:747) for every dead-lettered completion row — combining the per-child profile id with the exact Torah/Mishnah reference the child was studying in one string; pull_pipeline.dart fires sync_merge_router_halt with a bare profile_id; tutor_pin_service.dart fires tutor_pin_set with a bare profile_id; tutor_audit_log_writer.dart fires tutor_action_recorded with a 'target' field whose own documented shape is a resource path like 'profile/42.displayName' (line 130) — i.e. the profile id again, now attached to a description of what was changed; sync_orchestrator.dart fires sync_pull_failed and sync_listener_error with the raw exception's `.toString()`, which for Firestore permission/not-found errors routinely embeds the full document resource path (profiles/{id}/completions/{ref}). In release/profile builds analyticsServiceProvider resolves to the real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart), whose logEvent forwards `parameters` verbatim with zero redaction (firebase_analytics_service.dart:29-32) — so every one of these fires a real event to Google's servers. This is materially worse than the two baselined single-field leaks (bare sefaria_ref, bare profile_id in analytics_service.dart) because several of these sites combine per-child identity with content/action detail in one uncatalogued, unreviewed string, and remains a live COPPA/GDPR-K risk independent of the separately-baselined PV-3 consent-gating gap (fixing consent gating controls whether these fire at all, not what's inside them once a user has consented).
recommendation: Change AnalyticsService.logEvent's name parameter from bare String to a closed type sourced only from AnalyticsEvent (e.g. an extension type/sealed wrapper), add a Rule-0 grep/lint that fails CI on any `.logEvent(` call whose first argument isn't `AnalyticsEvent.<x>`, and triage the 7 cited sites: either drop the identifying parameter and keep these as AppLogger-only structured logs (most already have a parallel LogEvents-based AppLogger call right next to the analytics one), or promote them into AnalyticsEvent with PV-1-safe parameters (counts/enums/booleans only) and route error detail through a stable EH-5 error-code enum instead of `.toString()`.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (grep in make audit, or a working custom_lint rule) fails with file:line on any AnalyticsService.logEvent(...)/.logEvent( call whose event-name argument is not an AnalyticsEvent member
entity_key/profile_id/target/error-text parameters are removed, hashed, or replaced with a coarse enum at all 7 cited call sites

A regression test asserts FakeAnalyticsService-captured params for outbox_dead_lettered, merge_router_halt, pull_failed, listener_error, tutor_pin_set, and tutor_action_recorded never contain a raw profileId, sefariaRef, or exception string
docs/coding-standards.md PV-1 known-gaps list is either cleared for these sites or explicitly extended to name them

corrections: TutorAuditLogWriter (tutor_audit_log_writer.dart, the 7th site, 'target'/'grant_id' leak) has no constructor call anywhere in lib/ or test/ — it is currently dead/unwired code, not reachable in production today. The finding's 'sites: 7' should read 6 confirmed-reachable + 1 dormant; this does not change the verdict or severity since 6 live production leak sites remain independently confirmed, including one (entity_key) that combines profile_id with content identifier in a single string.

title: Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser
why: If currentUser is null when these fire (expired/revoked anonymous session, or a UI race), the `?.` swallows the call and the method returns a normally-completed Future<void> — no exception, no signal that nothing happened. The one real caller (features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:129-140 `linkGoogleProvider`/`linkEmailProvider`/`reauthenticateWithGoogle`) just awaits and reports success with nothing to double-check. That directly undercuts AU-1: linking must actually run against the anonymous uid so its offline data carries over; a silent no-op leaves the account anonymous while the user believes it's now permanent, and Identity Platform auto-deletes unlinked anonymous accounts after 30 days (AU-3's rationale), which can permanently orphan the child's offline learning history. Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.
recommendation: Add the same `if (user == null) throw ...` guard used elsewhere in this file before calling linkWithCredential/reauthenticateWithCredential in all three methods (ideally throwing the typed exception recommended in the companion EH-5 finding rather than another StateError). Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.
acceptance_criteria: linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken throw (not silently no-op) when currentUser is null.
New red-first unit tests in firebase_auth_gateway_impl_test.dart cover the null-currentUser case for all 3 methods and pass.
Existing 'links credential when signed in' tests for the same methods stay green.

corrections: The "one real caller ... just awaits and reports success" framing is wrong for 2 of 3 sites: linkWithGoogleIdToken/linkWithEmailAndPassword are dead code with no UI entry point in lib/ (only exercised by unit tests). The 3rd (reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken) is live but its only real call path guarantees currentUser is non-null, and the downstream deleteCurrentUser() call already guards null with a thrown StateError, so the claimed silent-orphan-account scenario has no actual path through the app today. The defect (missing guard, inconsistent with sibling methods) is real and worth fixing defensively, but severity should be P2 (design debt/defensive hygiene), not P1 (user-visible defect).

Downgrade from P1 to P2 (design debt, not currently user-visible) and CONFIRMED to SUSPECTED. 2 of the 3 cited sites (lines 218, 238 — linkWithGoogleIdToken/linkWithEmailAndPassword) are dead code with no UI caller anywhere in lib/ (no Link Account screen exists). The 1 reachable site (line 226, reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken, called from account_actions.dart:286) is guarded downstream by Firebase's server-side recent-login enforcement in deleteCurrentUser(), which is caught and surfaced as an error rather than causing silent corruption/security bypass. The underlying code smell (missing null guard vs. sibling pattern) is real and worth fixing before the link feature ships, but the P0-adjacent 'orphans child's offline learning history' consequence described in 'why' is not reachable today.

title: Scope DAO id-based get/update/delete methods to profileId — goal_dao, bookmark_dao, learning_order_dao, stage_dao, and BaseDao.getById all mutate by bare row id

evidence.quote:
Future<Row?> getById(int id) {
    final query = select(table)..where((t) => idColumn(t).equals(id))
**Enforcement:** `make audit` flags any user-DB table without a `profileId` column.

why: Every table these DAOs sit on (curriculum_tracks, bookmarks, goals, learning_order, stage_definitions, …) declares profileId only in a secondary `uniqueKeys`/`@TableIndex`, not in Drift's actual `primaryKey` — the real PK is a bare autoincrement `id` (verified directly in lib/core/database/tables/*.dart). docs/coding-standards.md:663-665 names this an explicit invariant ("No user-facing Drift table may use a single-column autoincrement primary key without also specifying profileId as part of a composite key override") and claims it is enforced by `make audit`; the learning_tracker/Makefile audit target (22 numbered greps, lines 277-505) has no such check — the claim is false. Because the PK is bare id, `getById`/`update…().replace()`/`delete…(id)` never filter by profileId, so any caller that obtains a foreign profile's numeric id (stale provider state after a profile switch, a sync-merge bug, a crafted id) can read/overwrite/delete another profile's row. This is not theoretical: lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart's updateGoal/deleteGoal fetch `goalDao.getGoalById(goalId)` and then unconditionally mutate/delete without ever comparing `existing.profileId` to the repository's own bound profile — the DAO provides zero defense-in-depth and this caller adds none either. (Contrast: bookmark_repository_impl.setBookmark re-derives the id via a profileId-checked lookup first, so it's safe — the inconsistency across callers is exactly what a shared, enforced invariant is supposed to prevent.)
recommendation: Add profileId as an explicit parameter to every id-based get/update/delete DAO method in this batch (or drop BaseDao.getById/replace-by-id entirely in favor of profileId-qualified variants) and filter the WHERE/replace target on it. Fix or remove the false claim at docs/coding-standards.md:689, and either wire a real Rule-0 check (a grep over lib/core/database/tables/*.dart primaryKey declarations, or a lint over DAO WHERE clauses) into `make audit`, or downgrade the doc's [E] tag to [P].
acceptance_criteria: A new test (e.g. in goal_dao_test.dart / bookmark_dao_test.dart / stage_dao_test.dart) creates two profiles, inserts a row for profile A, calls the DAO's update/delete method with profile A's row id from a profile-B context, and asserts the row is unchanged / the call is rejected.

goal_repository_impl.updateGoal/deleteGoal (and any other caller found via `grep -rn 'DaoBaseDao\|getGoalById\|getBookmarkById\|getLearningOrderById\|getStageDefinitionById'`) verify existing.profileId against the caller's bound profile before mutating.
docs/coding-standards.md:689 either matches a real `make audit` check or is corrected to state the gap.

corrections: The finding says the enforcement claim at coding-standards.md:689 is false because `make audit` has no such check — true, but incomplete: a separate target `make schema-check` (tool/schema_check.dart) implements a related, looser profileId-in-key check for a whitelisted subset of tables, and its own source comments independently corroborate that Goals is a known, unenforced gap. This strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

title: Wrap point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, and track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder in a transaction

evidence.quote:
for (final d in fallbackDefaults) {
        await insertConfig(

for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {
      await into(trackLearningOrder).insert(

why: None of these three multi-row writers is wrapped in `db.transaction()`. If the app is killed/backgrounded mid-loop (routine on mobile), the row set is left partially written. The clearest user-visible case: track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder is called from saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder (lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart) with the full reordered item list — tens of refs for a masechtos reorder. A crash partway through leaves some refs at their new sortOrder and others at stale values, silently scrambling the track's learning order with no error surfaced. point_config_dao.seedDefaults has a similar exposure (a stage left with no PointConfig row); study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults is lower-risk because isStudyDay() defaults a missing row to 'study' anyway.
recommendation: Wrap each loop body in `await db.transaction(() async { ... })` so the whole seed/reorder either fully applies or fully rolls back.
acceptance_criteria: seedDefaults (both DAOs) and upsertOrder execute inside db.transaction().
A regression test forces a failure on a middle iteration (e.g. a duplicate/invalid row) and asserts none of the batch's rows persisted (all-or-nothing).

title: Make SacredWindowDao's cache replace atomic — clearAll()+insertAll() must be one transaction, not the caller's fire-and-forget chain
why: The DAO's own doc comment says '[clearAll] + [insertAll] are called together... Expects the caller to have called [clearAll] first so the table stays coherent' — but the DAO exposes no atomic way to do that, and the only caller (SacredWindowRepository._persistToDb) chains them with `.then(...).ignore()`: unawaited, no transaction, errors silently discarded. If the process dies (routine on mobile backgrounding) between clearAll() completing and insertAll() completing, sacred_window_entries is left empty. That table is the documented source of truth for 'background notification-fire-time checks... without the Flutter engine' (DNI-367) — an empty table means Sacred Time notification suppression silently fails open on next cold-start check, with no error anywhere (`.ignore()` explicitly suppresses it). invalidate() → _persistToDb runs on every location/timezone change and app resume, so the window isn't rare.
recommendation: Add a single `SacredWindowDao.replaceAll(List<SacredWindowEntriesCompanion> entries)` that wraps clearAll+insertAll in one `db.transaction()`, and have sacred_window_repository.dart call that instead of the `.then().ignore()` chain. If fire-and-forget is intentional, at minimum log the failure via AppLogger instead of `.ignore()`.
acceptance_criteria: SacredWindowDao exposes an atomic replaceAll(); sacred_window_repository.dart no longer calls clearAll()/insertAll() separately.
A test makes insertAll throw mid-write inside replaceAll and asserts the table still holds the PREVIOUS rows (no empty-table window), not a partially-cleared state.

corrections: Downgrade P1 -> P2: the 'silent notification-suppression failure' consequence is aspirational, not live — grep confirms `sacredWindowDao.getAll()` is called nowhere in lib/ outside its own DAO/tests; isWindowActive() only consults the in-memory cache. The DB-2 violation itself (non-transactional, unawaited, .ignore()'d clear+insert) is real and should stay filed, but as design debt tied to the AC-26.24-req-4 background-read feature landing later, not as a currently reachable user-visible defect.

title: Wrap TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder's per-row insert loop and its repository call sites in one transaction/batch

evidence.quote:
Future<void> upsertOrder(int trackId, List<String> refs) async {
    for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {

why: upsertOrder writes N rows via an awaited for-loop with no db.transaction()/db.batch() wrapper, and its only callers (saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault) then make a second, entirely separate write (stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction either. A user reordering a full masechta/seder (which can be dozens to hundreds of refs) who has the app killed mid-reorder (OS memory pressure, backgrounding kill — routine on mobile) is left with a partially-old/partially-new sortOrder sequence and no error anywhere. getByTrack() then feeds that corrupted order straight into the daily learning projection, producing skipped or repeated study segments with zero user-visible signal that anything went wrong. Even when upsertOrder itself completes, dying before the separate stampReorderAt call leaves a stale lastReorderAt, breaking the reorder-amnesty logic documented at architecture §10.1. This is discovered via track_learning_order_dao_test.dart (in this batch), which covers the happy path only and has no test for interrupted/partial writes.
recommendation: Replace the for-loop in upsertOrder with a single db.batch((b) { for (...) b.insert(trackLearningOrder, ..., onConflict: ...); }) — Drift batches are atomic, satisfying DB-2 and DB-3 in one change. In the repository, wrap the order-write + stampReorderAt call of saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault in one _database.transaction(...) so the pair commits or rolls back together.
acceptance_criteria: TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder issues one db.batch() instead of an awaited per-row loop.
saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each wrap their order-write + stampReorderAt call in a single db.transaction().
New regression test asserts the reorder write is all-or-nothing (e.g. inject a failure partway through a multi-ref batch and assert zero rows changed / the pre-reorder order is intact).

No Rule-0 checker exists yet for this class of bug (DB-2/DB-3 are [P]ending) — note the gap; a grep for `for (` followed within a few lines by `await into(` or `await (db.update`/`await (db.delete` inside lib/core/database/daos/**/*.dart would catch this pattern cheaply.

corrections: Note for orchestrator (not a reason to kill): a closely related/possibly overlapping finding exists elsewhere in the audit (grp-117 'Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the order write', and grp-115) covering the same stampReorderAt-not-in-transaction defect from a different chunk -- worth deduping against high-007's DB-2 portion during merge, though high-007 additionally and correctly captures the distinct DB-3 per-row-loop defect in upsertOrder that those do not.

title: Add a schema-version floor guard for UserDatabase — onUpgrade has no path below v25

evidence.quote:
onUpgrade: (Migrator m, int from, int to) async {
        if (from < 25) {

why: git log -p on user_database.dart shows onUpgrade previously handled `if (from < 3)` through `if (from < 23)`; commit 9612d7a0 deleted that whole range and its own diff changes the docstring from '...schemaVersion bumped to 12; all old migration steps deleted' to describing a second 'W3.19 rebuild' wipe-install boundary. Today onUpgrade only starts at `from < 25`. database_provider.dart opens UserDatabase directly via driftDatabase(name: dbName) with no version-floor check at all — unlike ContentDatabase, which SeedManager guards with an explicit version comparison plus atomic replace before Drift ever touches it. Any real device whose local user_database.db is still at a schemaVersion below 25 will, on next launch, run onUpgrade(from=<old>, to=32): none of the intervening table-rename/profileId/FK changes apply, but Drift still stamps PRAGMA user_version=32 afterward — the on-disk schema stays frozen at its old shape while every DAO assumes v32's shape, so the first query throws 'no such column'/'no such table', or silently misreads a same-named-but-differently-typed column. coding-standards.md states as a current fact (2026-07-02) that 'the user DB is at schemaVersion 32 with real on-device data and no server backup', which is exactly the population this gap would hit. What would confirm real-world exposure: crash telemetry for 'no such column'/'no such table' immediately post-update, or checking whether any distributed build ever shipped schemaVersion 2-24 to non-dev devices before the WS7/v25 bump.
recommendation: Add a pre-open guard (mirroring SeedManager's pattern) that reads PRAGMA user_version via raw sqlite3 before handing the file to Drift; if it's below the lowest version this onUpgrade body actually handles, run a documented recovery path (backup + fresh onCreate) instead of letting Drift silently half-upgrade. Longer term, adopt DB-4's drift_schemas/ + migrateAndValidate tests so a future 'delete old migration steps' edit fails CI instead of shipping silently.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test opens a DB stamped with a low PRAGMA user_version (e.g. 2) and asserts the app either migrates it correctly through to 32 or safely detects-and-recovers — it must never end up with user_version=32 stamped over pre-v25 table shape.
database_provider.dart (or a new guard module) checks on-disk PRAGMA user_version against a documented MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION before opening via Drift.
DB-4's drift_schemas/ export + generated migration tests land so a future deletion of an `if (from < N)` block fails CI.

But the P0 "real device data corruption" claim rests on a premise the finding never checked: docs/linear-status.

The evidence quotes check out (schemaVersion=32, onUpgrade starts at from<25, no floor guard in database_provider.dart), but the P0 "data-corruption" claim rests entirely on "any real device...still at schemaVersion below 25" being reachable. docs/product-rules.md:183 states plainly: "Pre-launch
corrections: Quoted lines all exist verbatim and the commit history claim (9612d7a0 resetting schemaVersion 23→1, W3.19 "wipe-install boundary" rebuild) is accurate. The defect is not in the quotes but in the unverified "real device exposure" narrative: docs/linear-status.md ("wipe-install boundary...acceptable") and docs/product-rules.md ("Pre-launch — no live users") directly contradict the P0 data-loss framing, and the finding duplicates baselined known-gap #9 (missing drift_schemas/migration tests at v32) rather than surfacing a distinct novel defect.

Evidence quotes are accurate as cited, but the finding omits docs/product-rules.md:183 ("Pre-launch — no live users") which directly contradicts the "real device" exposure claim, and omits that the v25 floor was an intentional, already-executed migration boundary (see commits 9612d7a0 and 688fa74c) rather than an accidental gap.

title: Wrap DeviceRegistryDatabase.removeAccount's delete + state-clear in a transaction()

evidence.quote:
for (var i = 1; i < group.length; i++) {
        removed += await removeAccount(group[i].accountId);

why: removeAccount's own docstring says it clears lastActiveAccountId 'so the next launch does NOT silently auto-activate an arbitrary fallback account against a dangling pointer (D10)' — but the delete and the pointer-clear are two separately-awaited statements with no db.transaction() around them. If the process dies between them (routine on Android when a backgrounded app is reclaimed, and account removal is exactly the kind of action a user triggers then backgrounds), the delete commits but the clear never runs, leaving deviceState.lastActiveAccountId pointing at a row that no longer exists — the exact D10 state device_registry_test.dart's 'removeAccount clears it when removing the ACTIVE account (D10)' test checks for, just reached through a crash path the in-memory test can't simulate. dedupeByEmail compounds this by calling removeAccount N times in an unwrapped loop, so a mid-run crash also leaves a partially-merged duplicate-account state. Every other multi-write DAO in this codebase (stage_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, user_profile_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart) wraps its writes in transaction() — this file is the outlier.
recommendation: Wrap removeAccount's body in `await transaction(() async { ... })`; wrap dedupeByEmail's per-group removal loop in one enclosing transaction (or a single batched delete) so a crash mid-merge can't leave a partially-deduped state.
acceptance_criteria: removeAccount and dedupeByEmail are wrapped in transaction()/batch(); a new test forces an exception between the delete and the state-clear and asserts neither write applied.
DB-2's Pending checker (audit grep for ≥2 awaited writes with no enclosing transaction() in a DAO method body) returns zero for this file.

corrections: Third evidence line cites device_registry_database.dart:185 but the quoted two-line snippet actually starts at line 184 (`for (var i = 1; ...)`) with line 185 being the second line only — off-by-one, not load-bearing.

The finding's "why" overstates impact: it claims the dangling lastActiveAccountId reaches "the exact D10 state" with harmful auto-activation, but session_persistence_service.dart:79-110 (resolveActiveAccountId) validates the pointer via findById() before trusting it and safely falls back otherwise — identical behavior to the properly-cleared case. Likewise dedupeByEmail's partial-merge risk is self-healing via the "One-shot per sign-in" re-scan at sign_in_controller.dart:428-433, not a lasting corruption. The rule violation (missing transaction wrap) is real; the claimed severity of harm is not.

Quotes/lines at device_registry_database.dart:111,114,185 are accurate (185 is the 2nd line of a 2-line quote starting at 184 — trivial). The 'why' section's central claim — that the transaction gap causes silent auto-activation of an arbitrary fallback account on a dangling D10 pointer — is refuted by session_persistence_service.dart:79-110 (resolveActiveAccountId), called from account_bootstrap.dart:30 at every launch: it validates the pointer via findById() and falls back to an arbitrary account identically regardless of whether the pointer is null or dangling. Severity corrected from P1 to P3; acceptance criteria's crash-injection test would need to additionally show a behavioral difference from the existing fallback path to justify anything higher than hygiene-level.

title: Add profileId FK+CASCADE to 6 tables — tutored-mirror wipe currently orphans a mirrored child's data
rule: profileId-in-PK Invariant / DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity, FK-cascade discipline)

evidence.quote: the learner_profiles row cascades to all mirrored rows in completions, ... curriculum_tracks, etc. No explicit child-row deletion is needed.
The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` on every child table (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, bookmarks, goals, etc.)
// `outbox` has no FK — without this its pending pushes for the deleted profile would survive.

why: None of these 6 tables declare `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` on their profileId column (every sibling table that IS correctly protected does). `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile()` compensates by explicitly deleting from all 6 before removing the profile row — the team clearly knows about this gap. But `TutoredMirrorWipeService.wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors/wipeRevokedMirrors` (used on tutor grant revoke/resign, tutor sign-out, and the D18 revoke-reconcile path) does NOT replicate that compensation — it only calls `ProfileDao.deleteTutoredMirrorByGrantId`, a bare delete of the `learner_profiles` row, while its own top-of-file comment incorrectly asserts universal FK cascade covering `curriculum_tracks, etc.`. `tutored_pull_service.dart` (line 99, 'a point_configs FK violation') confirms these tables are actually populated for a live mirror. Net effect: when a tutoring relationship ends, the tutored child's mirrored curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs rows silently persist on the tutor's device forever — a child-privacy data-retention failure that contradicts the code's own stated invariant, with no error or log to reveal it.
recommendation: Either (a) add `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` to profileId on all 6 tables (schema migration + schema export per DB-4), or (b) make `TutoredMirrorWipeService` explicitly delete from all 6 tables before removing the `learner_profiles` row, mirroring `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile`'s existing pattern (no migration needed, lower risk, matches established precedent). Fix the false comment either way.
acceptance_criteria: New regression test: after wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors, querying curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/outbox/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs WHERE profileId = <wiped id> returns 0 rows.
tutored_mirror_wipe_service.dart's header comment no longer claims universal FK cascade for tables that don't have it.

tool/schema_check.dart (or a new companion checker) flags any core/database/tables profileId column lacking a `.references(LearnerProfiles, ...)` FK, so a future new table can't silently reintroduce the gap.

corrections: The "rule" field's mapping is imprecise: I searched coding-standards.md in full and neither DB-6 nor the profileId-in-PK Invariant actually mentions FK cascade/onDelete behavior anywhere (grep for "cascade|onDelete|foreign key" in the doc returns zero hits) — DB-6 is about local-first write/watch/reconcile, and profileId-in-PK is about composite-PK column presence, not delete-cascade semantics. The underlying defect is real and well-evidenced (verified by direct code reading, not just quotes), but it isn't actually a violation of the two named rules' literal text — it's closer to an unstated data-integrity/child-privacy principle. Also worth flagging for the fix-author: outbox's inclusion in the "6 tables" is less certain — code comments suggest tutored-profile pushes are drain-guarded (never sent), so it's not fully confirmed outbox rows are ever created for a tutored mirror in the first place, though this doesn't undermine the other 5 tables.

Rule citation is imprecise: "profileId-in-PK Invariant" (composite-PK requirement) and DB-6 (local-first sync pattern) don't literally mandate FK-cascade; no coding-standards.md rule is explicitly titled "FK-cascade discipline" — closest textual anchor is the Privacy & Child Data section's general concern about orphaned privacy-sensitive child data. Also, the profile_repository_impl.dart:232 quote actually starts at line 230 ("...FK-cascade ordering. `outbox` has no FK — without this") and continues to 231, a 2-line citation offset. Neither issue undermines the underlying defect, which is real and well-evidenced.

title: Add UNIQUE(profileId, ulid) to PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions — sync merge can double-credit a child's points
rule: DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity) / profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement
why: PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions both carry a `ulid` column documented as "cross-device id for append-only cloud sync" — the exact same purpose LearningLedger's `ulid` serves, where it is protected by a real `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` @TableIndex. Neither PointsLedger nor RewardRedemptions has any uniqueKeys/@TableIndex at all. PointsLedgerMerger's own comment says entries are "deduplicated on ulid via INSERT-OR-IGNORE," but points_balance_dao.dart's insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent actually does a manual SELECT-then-INSERT with no DB constraint backing it — a classic TOCTOU race. If two merge calls for the same ulid ever interleave (concurrent pulls, a retried tutored pull, a future refactor that parallelizes merges), a duplicate row lands; reDeriveBalanceFromLedger sums ALL ledger deltas, so the child's points balance silently becomes wrong — violating the table's own documented invariant that balance is "the authoritative denormalised sum of all ledger entries."
recommendation: Add `@TableIndex(name: 'points_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true)` to PointsLedger and an equivalent unique index to RewardRedemptions (mirroring learning_ledger.dart), ship as a schema migration, and switch insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent to rely on that constraint (insertOnConflictDoNothing) instead of a separate SELECT.
acceptance_criteria: Schema migration adds the unique index to points_ledger and reward_redemptions, with committed schema export + generated migration test (DB-4).
Regression test: calling the merge path twice concurrently (Future.wait) with the same ulid results in exactly one row and exactly one balance credit.

corrections: The "rule" field's sub-clause "profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement" is the finding author's own paraphrase/inference, not verbatim text from DB-6 in coding-standards.md (DB-6 literally only mandates local-first write/watch/reconcile, not unique-index requirements). This does not undermine the finding's core, independently-verified defect.

title: Fix ScheduleSpec.weekly/.rolling to throw ArgumentError instead of assert() (silently unenforced in release builds)

evidence.quote: Throws [ArgumentError] when [daysOfWeek] is empty or contains values

why: WeeklySchedule and RollingSchedule enforce their invariants with Dart `assert()`, which the compiler strips out of release builds entirely (only active in debug/profile). Both factory doc comments explicitly promise 'Throws ArgumentError' — that promise is false in the exact build users run. `fromParts` (same file, line 63) feeds `daysOfWeek ?? const []` directly into `WeeklySchedule(...)` whenever the DB/JSON column is null, and the independent JSON codec path in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:346-349 does the same for a missing `days_of_week`/`days` key, wrapped in a try/catch that only rescues the debug-mode AssertionError — in release it silently produces a `WeeklySchedule([])`. A stage with an empty day-list never matches any weekday, so its chazara review permanently stops being scheduled with no error, no log, and no user-facing signal.
recommendation: Replace both asserts with explicit `if (...) throw ArgumentError(...)` (matching the pattern already used correctly by ScopeLevel/StageOrder/Pin/DayKind/CalendarSystem in the same directory) so the invariant holds in release builds too.
acceptance_criteria: ScheduleSpec.weekly([]) and ScheduleSpec.rolling(0)/.rolling(-1) throw ArgumentError when run under `flutter test` compiled in release/profile mode (or any assert-disabled run), not just debug.

New test/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec_test.dart exists and is wired into the test suite, covering empty/out-of-range daysOfWeek, non-positive windowSize, and fromParts with a null daysOfWeek column.
AG-5 mirroring restored: lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart has a corresponding test file (currently missing).

corrections: Rule citation 'EH-4' is a loose fit — EH-4's actual text concerns typed catch clauses / throwing only Exception-Error subclasses, not assert()-vs-ArgumentError release-mode stripping. The more relevant standard is the docstring's own documented contract plus AG-5 (missing test mirror), both correctly cited. Does not change the verdict since the defect and its evidence are independently confirmed.

The "why" narrative's claim that this bug causes chazara scheduling to silently stop is not supported — scheduler_engine.dart's actual scheduling decision reads `daysOfWeek` from raw JSON via SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl, never through ScheduleSpec/WeeklySchedule, so the assert-vs-throw defect cannot produce that consequence. Real impact is confined to `StageDefinition`/`.schedule` consumers (edit/export screens) via `_rowToModel`/`fromParts`, where release mode yields `WeeklySchedule([])` while debug mode's `catch (_)` swallows the AssertionError into `DelaySchedule(0)` — a data-model inconsistency, not a scheduling outage. The cited rule EH-4 (typed catch clauses / never catch Error subtypes) does not match this defect class; the actual violation is an undocumented (in coding-standards.md, "assert" appears nowhere) assert-vs-explicit-validation contract break.

title: Fix CurriculumLabel.item breadcrumb/parent modes to resolve ancestor Hebrew names, not just the leaf's
rule: hebrew-terms.md §6/§10 (Hebrew-Terms domain-term invariant); Rule 5 (CurriculumLabelRenderer is the sole rendering path)

evidence.quote: : rawValue)   // named-level fallback when hebrewName is null

case CurriculumLabelMode.breadcrumb:
  return CurriculumLabelRenderer.renderForItem(_item!, useHebrew: useHebrew, fullPath: true, ...);

why: renderForItem(fullPath: true) — the function backing CurriculumLabel.item(mode: .breadcrumb) — only knows the leaf ContentItem's own displayNameHe; hebrewNames is filled only at the last index, so renderValue's named-level branch falls back to the raw storage-key value ('Seder Zeraim', 'Berakhot') for every ancestor segment whenever useHebrew=true. CurriculumLabel.item's breadcrumb and parent cases call renderForItem/renderParentForItem without ever supplying hebrewNamesPerSegment — unlike the async curriculum_label_providers.dart path (renderedDisplayForRef/renderedBreadcrumbForRef), which correctly builds ancestor names via curriculumContentProvider. This is reachable today at step_starting_position.dart:211-217, part of add_track_flow_screen's starting-position picker used for every curriculum: with Hebrew Terms on, selecting a leaf under a named ancestor (any Mishnayos masechta, any Chumash sefer, Mussar sefer, etc.) shows a mixed-script breadcrumb like 'Seder Zeraim › ברכות › פרק א' instead of 'זרעים › ברכות › פרק א' — English proper names leaking into a Hebrew-mode screen, the exact class of defect already fixed under IL-2/IL-5/IL-7/PP-5. renderParentForItem's own doc comment and the existing test 'renderParentForItem on a chapter returns the Sefer (Hebrew)' (curriculum_label_renderer_test.dart) already document the raw-fallback contract and assert the English string 'Genesis' as 'expected' — the bug is that curriculum_label.dart's callers never satisfy that contract's precondition (supplying hebrewNamesPerSegment), so the documented fallback leaks into production UI instead of being avoided.
recommendation: Give CurriculumLabel.item's breadcrumb/parent modes a path to ancestor Hebrew names: either route them through the existing async renderedBreadcrumbForRefProvider(item.sefariaRef)/renderedParentForRefProvider(item.sefariaRef) (which already do this correctly via curriculumContentProvider), or thread a hebrewNamesPerSegment lookup into renderForItem/renderParentForItem the same way curriculum_label_providers.dart's _hebrewNamesForPath does.
acceptance_criteria: New widget test pumps CurriculumLabel.item(item, mode: CurriculumLabelMode.breadcrumb) for a curriculum with 2 named ancestor levels (e.g. Mishnayos) with Hebrew Terms on, and asserts every rendered segment is Hebrew script — no raw Latin/ASCII ancestor names.
Test fails on current code and passes once the fix lands; add the analogous case for CurriculumLabelMode.parent.

corrections: The finding's 'sites: 2' is loosely justified: only ONE concrete UI call site currently exercises the bug (step_starting_position.dart:211, mode=breadcrumb); CurriculumLabelMode.parent has no current call site in lib/ (confirmed via grep), so 'sites: 2' should be read as '2 broken render modes' rather than '2 live call sites' — a minor overstatement that does not affect the core defect's validity or severity.

title: Align readUseHebrewCalendar's stale '?? false' default with HebrewDatePreference.defaultValue=true
rule: Evans/DRY (invariant re-derived in two places) — no single rule ID; data-consistency correctness bug

why: outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:222 calls readUseHebrewCalendar() inside pushUiPreferencesSnapshot(), which _writeAndPushSnapshot() (preference_providers.dart) fires after every write to ANY sibling UI preference. title: Add the IL-1 sentinel-0 guard to UseHebrewDate/ShowNikudPref/CurrentTransliterationVariant/CurrentFontSize in preference_providers.dart
rule: SM-2/SM-3 (notifier state consistency across rebuilds) — documented bug class (IL-1) only partially fixed

evidence.quote:
if (profileId == 0 && _hasBindingForRealProfile) {
      // Transient sentinel — keep the last valid state.

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(hebrewDatePreferenceProvider);

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(nikudPreferenceProvider);

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(textDisplayPreferenceProvider);

why: The file's own comment documents that activeProfileIdProvider transiently emits sentinel 0 during the offline-signup DB switch (ref.invalidate(userDatabaseProvider)) before settling back to the real profile id. corrections: All four site line citations are off by exactly one line: the finding cites the `build() {` signature line (128/148/213/234) instead of the actual quoted `final profileId = ...` line, which is one line below (129/149/214/235 respectively). The quoted text itself is verbatim-correct at the corrected line numbers; this is a cosmetic citation offset, not a fabrication.

All four cited line numbers (128, 148, 213, 234) are off by exactly one line low -- the quoted two-line text actually starts at 129, 149, 214, and 235 respectively (each cited line lands on the build() signature line just above the quoted watch calls). title: Delete the dead TextDisplayPreferences singleton; repoint the tests that exercise it onto CurrentFontSize/ShowNikudPref

The "sites": 2 count undercounts by one -- a third exercise of the dead singleton exists at epic_02_content_test.dart:904-919 ("TextDisplayPreferences.showNikud defaults to true and persists"), and text_display_screen_test.dart:41 setUp is a fourth minor touch-point (harmless no-op but still worth folding into the fix). title: Redact TransactionalEmail.plaintextBody before logging in LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send()
rule: Child-privacy logging hygiene (PV-family principle) — breaks the PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys contract in core/logging/logger.dart that the same function's sibling field already relies on

evidence.quote: '$tutorEmail has declined your invitation to tutor $childName.\n\n'

PiiRedactor.redactFields() only blanks values whose KEY is in the 49-entry sensitiveKeys allowlist (logger.dart:203-251) — 'body' is not in it, even though 'to'/'recipient'/'email_to' were deliberately added and regression-tested (test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart:271-304, tag V2-R5 C2) for the exact same call site two lines above. Extend the existing V2-R5 C2 test group in test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart to cover the debug() 'Payload' call the same way it already covers the warning() call.

A new/updated test in test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart fails against current logger.dart and passes after the fix
flutter analyze and make ci remain green

title: Fix unsafe `as int?`/`as num?` casts in TrackCodec.decode and GoalCodec.decode that throw instead of returning null
rule: EH-2/EH-4 decode() null-on-malformed contract + Nygard partial-failure
why: entity_codec.dart's decode() contract states it 'Returns null when required fields are missing or malformed — the merger must skip malformed rows rather than crash.' Every other numeric field read across all 15 files in this batch goes through FirestoreCodec.parseInt, built specifically because Firestore fields can arrive as String (its own docstring says so). These 3 sites bypass it with a bare `as` cast: if profile_id/track_id/target_percent ever arrives as anything but exactly int (or num, for target_percent)/null — e.g. a String from a hand-edited doc, an import script, or a legacy document — `as int?`/`as num?` throws instead of returning null. TrackConfigMerger.merge() and GoalMerger.merge() call `_codec.decode(row)` inside a `for` loop with no try/catch, and MergeRouter.dispatch (merge_router.dart:55) awaits merger.merge() with no try/catch either, so one malformed row throws out of the whole pull page mid-iteration, silently dropping every row after it and aborting the sync pass instead of just skipping the bad row.
recommendation: Replace `raw['profile_id'] as int?` / `raw['track_id'] as int?` with `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['profile_id'])` / `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['track_id'])` (the int.tryParse fallback lines become redundant and can be deleted). Add a `FirestoreCodec.parseDouble` helper mirroring parseInt and use it for GoalCodec's target_percent instead of the raw `as num?` cast.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: TrackCodec().decode({'profile_id': '5', 'track_id': '7', 'curriculum_id': 'x', 'activated_at': <iso>}) returns a TrackRow, not a thrown exception.
Unit test: GoalCodec().decode({...,'target_percent': '55'}) returns a GoalRow with targetPercent 55.0 instead of throwing.
grep for 'as int?' / 'as num?' / 'as double?' / 'as bool?' across lib/core/sync/codec/*.dart returns zero matches (wire into make audit).

corrections: None needed — evidence lines and quotes are exact. Addition: actual blast radius is larger than described — it aborts the whole multi-collection pull-on-launch pass (all subsequent steps: learner_profiles, goals, ledger, etc.), not merely 'silently dropping every row after it' within one page.

The GoalCodec.decode() citation (goal_codec.dart:77) is misleading: GoalMerger.merge() does NOT call `_codec.decode(row)` at all — GoalCodec.decode() is dead code, never invoked in production (only GoalCodec.encode() is used, for push). GoalMerger instead does its own inline parsing and independently has the identical unguarded-cast bug live at goal_merger.dart:91 (`(row['target_percent'] as num?)?.toDouble() ?? 100.0`), uncited by the finding. Net effect: the defect class is real and reachable for goals too, just at a different, uncited file/line than claimed; the fix recommendation (patch GoalCodec) would not actually fix the live goal bug. The TrackCodec evidence (2 of 3 cited sites) is fully solid and independently sufficient to uphold at P1.

Site 3 (goal_codec.dart:77) is not reachable the way the finding describes. GoalMerger.merge() never calls GoalCodec.decode() — it has its own independent, equally-unsafe cast at goal_merger.dart:91 (`(row['target_percent'] as num?)?.toDouble() ?? 100.0`), which IS reachable via the same unguarded merge-loop/pull-abort chain as the track_codec sites. GoalCodec.decode() itself is dead code in production (only exercised by test/sync/merge/goals_roundtrip_test.dart), so it should be fixed for contract-correctness/future-proofing but is not currently the live crash site — goal_merger.dart:91 is. Recommend adding goal_merger.dart:91 to the fix list (or replacing it entirely with `_codec.decode(row)` + `FirestoreCodec.parseDouble`) rather than treating goal_codec.dart:77 as reachable as originally written. Sites 1-2 (track_codec.dart:85,89) and the overall reachability/severity narrative for those two are fully confirmed as described.

title: Route LearningLedgerCodec.encode's completedAt through FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime instead of raw toIso8601String()
rule: Evans consistency (single documented UTC-safe conversion path) / data-integrity
why: Every other DateTime field in all 14 sibling codecs — and every other field in this very file (see decode() at line 84-86) — is pushed via FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime, which forces `.toUtc()` before serializing so the wire string always carries a 'Z' suffix. This one call skips it. entry.completedAt is read back from Drift's `dateTime()` column which, per the pinned drift-2.31.0 source (lib/src/runtime/types/mapping.dart:174, default storeDateTimesAsText=false, not overridden anywhere in this repo), decodes via `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(unixSeconds*1000)` with no isUtc:true — producing a **local**, non-UTC-flagged DateTime even though the original value came from DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(). `.toIso8601String()` on a non-UTC DateTime omits the 'Z'/offset entirely. When a different device (a parent or tutor on a different device/timezone — an explicitly supported flow in this app, see tutor_grant_codec.dart in this same batch) pulls the row, FirestoreCodec.parseDateTime's `DateTime.tryParse(raw)?.toUtc()` (used by learning_ledger_merger.dart) reinterprets the offset-naive string using the READING device's local offset rather than the writer's, shifting completedAt by the delta between the two devices' UTC offsets — potentially moving a ledger entry onto the wrong calendar day on the syncing device.
recommendation: Change line 67 to `'completed_at': FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime(model.completedAt),` to match every sibling codec.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: encode a LearningLedgerRow with a non-UTC-flagged completedAt (isUtc:false, simulating the Drift round-trip) and assert the resulting 'completed_at' string ends in 'Z' and represents the correct UTC instant.
learning_ledger_roundtrip_test.dart extended so decode(encode(x)) is timezone-independent (passes under a non-UTC ambient TZ).

corrections: The reachable path is broader than cited: not only the bulk-backfill path in local_data_upload_service.dart:261, but also the default per-completion save path in learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart (recordCompletion re-reads the row from Drift via getEntryById before encoding), so this bug triggers on essentially every live completion sync, not just bulk uploads.

title: Guard stage_definition/settings/goal merges against missing local track before FK-constrained insert
rule: Nygard (I/O ordering race) — FK integrity on merge; matches the fix already applied to bookmark/gamification_settings/study_day_config
why: lib/core/database/tables/stage_definitions.dart and goals.dart both declare `trackId => integer().references(CurriculumTracks, #id)()` — a real, enforced FK. If a stage_definition/settings/goal Firestore snapshot merges before its curriculum_tracks row exists locally (independent per-collection listeners, or first-launch pull on a restored device), the raw insert throws an uncaught SqliteException(787) and aborts merging the whole page. BookmarkMerger (drift_merge_store.dart:527 `if (track == null) { ...skip... }`), GamificationSettingsMerger (gamification_settings_merger.dart:128 `if (localTrack == null) continue;`) and StudyDayConfigMerger (study_day_config_merger.dart:66 `if (trackExists == null) continue;`) already guard this exact race by skipping and relying on the next (idempotent) pull to re-merge — the pattern was never generalized to stage_definition/settings/goal, which resolve the identical remote-track-id-fallback (`localTrack?.id ?? remoteTrackId`) without ever checking the fallback actually exists.

      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(

why: Every natural-key LWW merger applies the remote row (_store.upsert, which writes the entity table including its own updatedAt column) and THEN separately persists the SyncKv shadow timestamp (_store.persistUpdatedAt) as two independent awaited Drift writes with no enclosing db.transaction(). If the process dies between the two — an OS kill or force-quit on mobile is routine, not exotic — the entity row is left holding the remote's updatedAt while SyncKv still holds the pre-merge value. Any local edit made before the next successful sync now races a STALE local timestamp: a re-pulled, unchanged remote row will look newer than the stale SyncKv record and DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer will silently let it overwrite the user's genuinely-newer local edit — no exception, no log, nothing to retry against. This is DB-2's 'crash mid-sequence leaves the DB half-written' failure applied to the LWW bookkeeping itself.
recommendation: Add a MergeStore.applyRemote(...) that wraps the entity write and its SyncKv persistUpdatedAt in one db.transaction() (or expose a transaction-scoped variant), and switch all 8 callers to it.
acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection/unit test: call upsert() alone (simulating a crash before persistUpdatedAt commits), then perform a legitimately-newer local edit to the same row, then re-merge the identical stale remote row — assert the local edit survives.

This does not change the verdict but the acceptance-criteria fault-injection test should target one of the unguarded 5 to reliably reproduce the failure.

title: Give OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard a generation token so stale-reclaim can't run concurrent drains

evidence.quote: // reclaim only inspects the *same instance's* private state we also

why: The single-flight guard is two plain fields (_draining/_drainingSince) with no per-invocation identity. In production, OutboxProcessor is built with unmodified defaults (outbox_providers.dart:98-105: pushTimeout/drainStaleAfter never overridden) and sync_orchestrator.dart fires a periodic drain every 60s forever (Timer.periodic(_periodicDrainInterval, ...)) while drainStaleAfter is 90s. Non-completion kinds are pushed one row at a time, individually awaited (up to 50 rows x ~18 kinds) — a real multi-kind backlog on a slow connection easily exceeds 90s. When that happens, the next periodic (or connectivity/lifecycle) trigger sees the guard as 'stale', resets it, and starts a second, genuinely concurrent `_doDrain()` while the first is still running — the code comment at line 206-211 only reasons about two *reclaimers* racing each other synchronously; it never accounts for the *original* stale-but-still-running drain's own `finally` unconditionally zeroing `_draining`/`_drainingSince` once it eventually completes, which can then let a THIRD trigger barge in on top of the second. This directly breaks the documented contract ('collapses them to one push round' / sync_orchestrator.dart:568 'the OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard collapses races with other triggers'), producing duplicate concurrent Firestore pushes and racy interleaved deleteRow/markAttempted calls that can double-count a row's attempts and dead-letter a recoverable failure roughly twice as fast as _maxAttempts=10 implies. The R6-13 regression test that targets exactly this code path never builds true overlap: every scenario releases and awaits the 'wedged' pipeline to full completion before the next drain runs (its own comment admits the limitation at line 1392/1396), so the actual race is untested.
recommendation: Replace the boolean+timestamp guard with a construct that can tell 'my invocation' apart from a later reclaimer — e.g. a monotonically increasing generation counter captured at acquire time, checked before `finally` clears state (`if (_generation == myGeneration) { _draining = false; ... }`), or switch to chaining onto the in-flight Future (a late caller awaits/joins the existing drain rather than racing a flag).
acceptance_criteria: New/updated unit test keeps the first drain's pipeline call parked on a Completer, advances the clock past drainStaleAfter, drives a second (reclaiming) drain to full completion, then completes the first — and asserts the pipeline was invoked exactly once for the outstanding rows, or that DAO state is never corrupted by true overlap.
Guard implementation carries a generation token (or equivalent) so a finally block from an earlier invocation cannot clear state established by a later one.

corrections: The finding's characterization of the R6-13 test as "never builds true overlap" is only partially accurate. title: Fix make audit check 15/15's self-comparing awk so cross-feature deep imports are ever detected

why: match($1,...) extracts the feature name from the FILE PATH ($1, e.g. 'dashboard'). match($0,...) is meant to extract the feature name of the IMPORTED module, but $0 is 'path:line:content' and $1 is a literal prefix of $0, so match($0,...) finds that same 'dashboard' substring inside the path prefix before it ever reaches the import statement — a[1] and b[1] are therefore always identical and 'if (a[1] != b[1])' can never be true for any input. The unawaited call site in completion_repository_impl.dart has a catch path instead of relying on the global zone error handler

corrections: The finding's "unhandled Future error" framing slightly overstates the silence: main.dart's runZonedGuarded + PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError DO catch this and route it through AppLogger.instance.handle() and Crashlytics (as a misleading fatal report), so it isn't fully log-less. But this doesn't rescue the finding: there's still no retry/reconciliation, no user-facing signal, and no test exercises the failure branch — the core defect (silent, permanent loss of the siyum credit with zero test coverage of the failure path) stands.</evidence_correction>

Severity should be downgraded from P1 to P2. The finding's "why" claims the failure would be "silently" absorbed with "no user-facing signal" and "no reconciliation job anywhere in lib/ to catch the gap." This overstates the risk: main.dart wraps app startup in runZonedGuarded (lines 15-34), and an uncaught error from an unawaited Future is delivered to that zone handler, which calls both `_crashlytics.recordError(error, stack, fatal: true)` and `AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack)`. So the exception is NOT silent — it is logged and reported fatal to Crashlytics, giving operators a signal (though not an automatic retry/reconciliation for the missed siyum credit). The rule citations (EH-2/EH-3) are also a loose fit: EH-3 concerns log-less *catch blocks*, and there is no catch block here at all; EH-2 concerns raw exceptions propagating into *presentation*, which doesn't happen since the zone handler intercepts before reaching UI. The underlying gap — no explicit local handling/retry for this specific invariant (B1 siyum credit) and no test exercising the failure path — is real design debt (P2: "design debt with stated concrete cost"), not the P1 "silent, unsignaled defect" the finding portrays.

The finding's framing of 'no user-facing signal' is accurate, but 'silently fails' slightly overstates the logging gap: main.dart wraps the app in runZonedGuarded, whose handler does route unhandled Future errors to AppLogger.instance.handle(...) and Crashlytics.recordError(fatal: true) — so the exception is NOT unlogged. This doesn't kill the finding: the underlying invariant break (siyum permanently not recorded, no retry, no scoped/contextual handling) is real and untested, which the finding's own recommendation and acceptance criteria already account for (explicitly asking for a catch path 'instead of relying on the global zone error handler').

why: ProfileRepositoryImpl wraps every _syncEngine?.pushLearnerProfile(...) call in a blanket catch(_) {} (createProfile:104-109, updateProfile:157-161, self-heal:321-336), on the premise that 'local write already succeeded (offline-first)' and the push will retry later. Per sync_providers.dart:75-78, when a tutor session is active, _syncEngine is instead a TutoredWriteRouter that turns pushLearnerProfile into a one-shot, non-retryable Cloud Function RPC (tutorEditProfile). title: Fix Makefile check 15/15 cross-feature-deep-import detector — awk comparison always matches a feature against itself

area: tooling (learning_tracker/Makefile `make audit` check 15/15) — found while triaging this batch's cross-feature imports against the Rule-2 baseline
why: match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b) scans the WHOLE grep -n line ('path:line:content'), so it always matches the importing file's own features/<name>/ segment first — the identical substring match($1,...) already captured into a[1] — because the file path precedes the import statement in that line. a[1] and b[1] are therefore always equal and the WARN branch can never fire, for any input; verified empirically by piping a real progress-to-learning cross-feature import line through the exact awk one-liner, which prints nothing instead of the intended warning. 'make audit ... PASSED — all 22 greps clean' and this audit's own baseline note that 'ALL current cross-feature deep-import edges are baselined' cannot be verified against reality for Rule 2 — the source list is empty by construction, not by absence of violations.
recommendation: Fix the awk to compare the import target's feature against the importing file's own feature — e.g. restrict the second match() to substr($0, length($1)+1) so it only scans the import-statement portion of the line — then re-run make audit and reconcile the resulting edge count against the digest's baseline claim, which today only actually covers check 14.

title: Fix the tautological awk comparison in make audit check 15 so cross-feature deep imports are ever reported
why: awk's match() finds the leftmost occurrence of `features/([^/]+)/` in $0, which for a `file:line:content` grep line is always inside the FILE PATH itself (it precedes the content). So a[1] (from $1, the path) and b[1] (from $0) are always derived from the same leading match and are always equal — `a[1] != b[1]` can never be true. I reproduced this directly: piping the real repo through the exact pipeline yields 0 lines even though 1186 lines match the pre-filter pattern, and manually evaluating the awk on a scheduler_providers.dart import line prints `a=scheduler b=scheduler` for an import that is unambiguously FROM `features/learning/`. recommendation: Rewrite the check-15 pipeline to compare the importing file's own feature (parsed once from $1) against the imported feature (parsed from the import statement/content portion only, e.g. by stripping $1 and the line number before matching), and add a fixture test (a temp file with a deliberate deep cross-feature import) asserting the check's exit/output actually flags it before merging any fix.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` check 15 prints at least one file:line when a deliberate cross-feature deep import is introduced in a throwaway test fixture.

title: Sync push payloads embed client-clock timestamps as the cross-device LWW ordering field instead of FieldValue.serverTimestamp()

evidence.quote:
the device with the
strictly newer timestamp wins.
// remote document carries a valid LWW timestamp. The merger

why: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's own Push/pull invariant says the device with the 'strictly newer timestamp' wins LWW races. Every updated_at value this batch's push payloads carry comes from `_clock.nowUtc()` (LocalDayClock, ultimately the device's own system clock) or a Drift-stored value stamped by the device clock at write time -- never FieldValue.serverTimestamp(). coding-standards.md's own FB-2 rationale names the exact failure: 'two devices with skewed clocks writing client timestamps make last-write-wins non-deterministic -- the faster clock always wins and silently overwrites newer data.' A device with a wrong/stuck system clock (common on hand-me-down or long-offline tablets, which this family-learning app explicitly supports offline) will have every goals/curriculum_tracks/settings/gamification_settings push either always lose or always win LWW races regardless of actual edit recency, silently discarding another device's real edits with no error surfaced anywhere.
recommendation: Route the LWW ordering field for mutable-document pushes through FieldValue.serverTimestamp() at the Firestore-gateway layer (the codebase already does this correctly for the separate synced_at field in firestore_gateway_impl.dart), keeping the client timestamp only as a local optimistic-ordering hint per FB-2's own wording. The fix site is core/sync/ (gateway + merge layer), outside this batch; these two files are the clearest evidence, not the fix location.
acceptance_criteria: FB-2 Rule-0 checker per coding-standards.md: audit grep asserting no DateTime.now()-derived value feeds a sync codec's ordering field, plus an emulator test asserting the persisted ordering field is a server Timestamp.
Extend test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart (or add a sibling test) with a case that sets one device's local clock backward and asserts its genuinely later edit still wins the LWW race.

corrections: The 'why' section is slightly incomplete: it omits that remoteIsNewer() falls back to the server-assigned synced_at as a tie-breaker within a +/-5s clock-skew window (drift_merge_store.dart, used by every LWW merger). This mitigates only near-simultaneous conflicting writes; it does not protect against the large clock skew the finding describes (stuck/wrong-date devices), so the core defect and reachability claim still hold. Worth folding this nuance into the finding's rationale/recommendation for accuracy, but it does not change the verdict.

The finding's 'always lose or always win... regardless of actual edit recency' slightly overstates the mechanism: DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart) has an undocumented-in-the-finding +/-5s clock-skew tie-break that consults the server-stamped synced_at field before falling back to client updated_at. This narrows the failure window to skew >5s but does not fix the underlying FB-2 violation for realistic 'wrong/stuck clock' devices, so the finding's conclusion still holds.

title: Fix learning_tracker/Makefile check 15/15 cross-feature-import awk — it can never detect a violation

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

why: grep -n emits 'path:line:content', so the file's own path (which always contains 'features/<owning-feature>/') appears in $0 BEFORE the import statement text. awk's match($0, /features\/([^/]+)\//, b) returns the FIRST match in the line — the file's own feature — not the imported feature, so b[1] always equals a[1] (both extracted from the same file-path segment) and the `a[1] != b[1]` guard can never be true. title: Fix the awk field-split bug in `make audit` check 15/15 that makes cross-feature-import detection a permanent no-op

evidence.quote: match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

why: Check 15/15's awk splits each `grep -rn` hit on ':' and calls match($1,...) for the file's own feature and match($0,...) for the import's feature, expecting them to differ on a real violation. title: Log and surface the swallowed exceptions in step_starting_position.dart._loadContent and step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry instead of silently stranding the user
why: step_starting_position.dart._loadContent catches everything and only flips _loading to false — it never logs via AppLogger and never sets an error flag. Since _containers/_leaves default to [], build() falls straight through to `_buildContainerList` with an EMPTY list and no CircularProgressIndicator, no error text, and no retry action: the user lands on a blank, silently-broken 'starting position' step of the Add-Track wizard with the Continue button permanently disabled (onPressed requires _selectedLeaf != null, which can never become non-null from an empty list) and zero indication anything went wrong. step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry has no catch at all (only `finally`) around two awaits, and every caller invokes it via `unawaited(...)`, so a thrown exception becomes an unhandled Future rejection with no AppLogger trail; the user instead sees the ALSO-hardcoded 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' fallback, which mislabels a real fetch/service failure as 'no data for this date'.

corrections: Site 2's claim of 'no AppLogger trail' is not accurate: main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded(), whose handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) (and Crashlytics.recordError) for any uncaught zone error, which includes unhandled Future rejections from unawaited(_refreshCalendarEntry()). So the exception IS logged globally, just without curriculumId/programKey context and without any widget-local error state — the user still only ever sees the hardcoded 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' fallback (confirmed at line ~426), which is the real, narrower defect at this site. Also note _refreshCalendarEntry has no catch block at all (only finally), so it isn't literally an 'empty/log-less catch' under EH-3's wording — the recommendation to 'log via AppLogger in both catches' requires adding a catch clause here, not fixing an existing one. Site 2 claim "a thrown exception becomes an unhandled Future rejection with no AppLogger trail" is inaccurate: main.dart's runZonedGuarded error handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) (and Crashlytics.recordError fatal:true) for any unhandled zone error, which includes errors from unawaited(_refreshCalendarEntry()) since it has no local catch. Site 2's premise is partly wrong: step_starting_position_calendar.dart's _refreshCalendarEntry has try/finally with no catch, called via unawaited(...), so any thrown exception propagates as an uncaught zone error — but main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded whose handler calls `AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack)` (main.dart:32) and reports to Crashlytics. why: grep -c 'expect(' on the file returns 0 — in 1482 lines, nothing can ever fail except a compile error (e.g. a renamed getter), which would abort the whole file rather than flag the specific key. The file's own docstring admits its purpose is purely to drive line-execution through lib/l10n/app_localizations_en.dart and _he.dart (5100+ generated lines each) for the CI-enforced coverage floor. docs/coding-standards.md states the 60% line-coverage floor is measured with 'generated files excluded', but .github/workflows/ci.yml's coverage-floor step runs `lcov --summary` directly on the raw lcov.info with no `lcov --remove` step anywhere in the repo (verified: no lcov --remove/genhtml exclude pattern exists in Makefile or ci.yml) — so generated files are NOT excluded in practice, and this file's 725-getter roll call launders thousands of auto-generated, logic-free lines into the numerator that the doc claims shouldn't count. Concrete cost: every new l10n key needs a manual line added here (already 725, and easy to forget silently since forgetting produces no failure), for a test that cannot catch a wrong translation, a missing plural case, or the exact ARB duplicate-key bug found elsewhere in this batch.
recommendation: Either (a) wire the promised exclusion into the CI coverage step (lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info 'lib/l10n/app_localizations_*.dart' '*.g.dart' ... before lcov --summary) and delete this file, or (b) if kept for its doc-verification role, replace the per-getter roll call with a real check (e.g. that every ARB key has a corresponding generated getter) instead of 1482 lines that assert nothing.
acceptance_criteria: CI's coverage-floor step excludes generated files from the denominator (matching the doc's claim) OR this file is deleted/replaced with an assertive test.
docs/coding-standards.md's 'generated files excluded' claim matches what .github/workflows/ci.yml actually does.

title: Broaden no_hardcoded_percent_in_chart_subtitle_test.dart regex to catch unsigned fabricated percentages
rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than the class of defect the source can actually reproduce)
why: The original defect (per the file's own docstring) was 'a static placeholder ... never computed at runtime' — the fix removed the number entirely. But the regression test only rejects the signed digit-percent shape ('+12%'/'-5%'). A future contributor could reintroduce the same never-computed-at-runtime fabrication as 'chartCumulativeProgressSubtitle: 12% higher than last week' (no sign) or as a non-percent fake stat ('12 more completions than last week'), and this test would pass, giving false confidence that the fix is intact.
