title: Type streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart's two catch blocks to Exception — bare Object catches swallow Error subtypes as warnings
why: Neither catch has an `on X` clause, so both also catch Dart Error subtypes (NoSuchMethodError, TypeError, RangeError, StateError) that signal genuine programming bugs, not recoverable runtime conditions — exactly what EH-4 says never to catch. A bug in StreakStateProvider or an unexpected state shape gets downgraded to a single logger.warning(...) call (not even error/critical) and the loop or stream quietly continues or ends — no crash, no Crashlytics report, nothing but a line in a 2000-entry ring buffer nobody reviews outside 'Send Diagnostic Logs'. This provider runs unconditionally in the app shell every session (per its own doc comment), so a regression here has zero blast-radius signal to catch it.
recommendation: Narrow both catches to `on Exception catch (e, st)` (or the specific exception types StreakStateProvider/AnalyticsService can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate to the zone's onError handler like the rest of the app.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch clauses in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart use `on Exception catch` (or a named typed exception), not bare `catch (e, st)`
streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's existing R6-3 tests still pass unchanged (they throw plain Exception, not Error)

corrections: Ran a probe test: querying a closed Drift NativeDatabase throws StateError (e is Error==true, e is Exception==false) — the exact scenario R6-3's stream-error test triggers via db.close(). Narrowing line 83's catch to `on Exception` lets that StateError escape and flips state.hasError to true, breaking the existing green test the finding claims 'still pass unchanged.' Doc comment (lines 34-37) also documents the swallow-all behavior as deliberate, not accidental. Downgrading severity/confidence accordingly; the inner catch (line 74) is a cleaner, lower-stakes instance of the same rule violation.

title: Guard CrashlyticsService's unawaited analytics calls with catchError — unguarded rejection can re-enter the runZonedGuarded fatal-error handler
why: main.dart wraps the whole app in runZonedGuarded whose error callback (lines 26-31) calls _crashlytics.recordError(...) — which is FirebaseCrashlyticsService.recordError, firing `unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...))` with no .catchError attached at either of the two sites cited. If the Firebase Analytics plugin call itself rejects (platform-channel failure, SDK not yet initialized, offline queue full), that unhandled Future error is delivered back into the very same Zone installed by runZonedGuarded, invoking the identical error callback again, which calls recordError again, firing another unawaited call — a self-feeding loop precisely at the moment (an active fatal-crash report) when the app's error-handling path most needs to be inert. Contrast with streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart in the same directory tree, which does guard its own fire-and-forget analytics call with `.catchError(...)` (line 63-70) — the inconsistency shows this omission wasn't a deliberate choice. Needs runtime confirmation: inject an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always rejects inside a runZonedGuarded harness and observe whether recordError re-enters.
recommendation: Add `.catchError((_, __) {})` (or route failures through AppLogger only) to both unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...)) calls in crashlytics_service.dart, matching the guard pattern already used in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Both fire-and-forget analytics calls in crashlytics_service.dart have an attached .catchError/try-catch so a rejected Future never re-enters the zone's onError
A regression test injects an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always throws, calls recordError once, and asserts it is not invoked a second time

corrections: main.dart citation line is off by 4: the quoted `_crashlytics.recordError(error, stack, fatal: true);` is actually at line 31 (comments above it push it down from the cited 27). Quote text itself is exact and uniquely locatable, so this is a minor citation drift, not fabrication.

title: Inject an overridable clock into streakMilestoneAnalyticsObserverProvider instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
why: The observer instantiates `const SystemLocalDayClock()` directly rather than watching an injectable clock — the codebase already has this seam elsewhere (e.g. outbox_providers.dart reads `ref.watch(localDayClockProvider)`). Because the observer can't be handed a fixed clock in tests, the happy-path test has to anchor seeded data to real `DateTime.now()` and then poll every 20ms for up to 5 real seconds waiting for the milestone to fire, instead of asserting deterministically against a fixed instant. The test's own comment documents this was already a source of past flakiness ('silently breaks the moment the calendar advances', 'failed in isolation') — the current polling approach is less likely to fail, not deterministic, and burns up to 5 real seconds per run.
recommendation: Thread a LocalDayClock through the provider (watch a clock provider, mirroring outbox_providers.dart) so tests can override with a fixed clock and assert the milestone fires on an exact expected tick without polling.
acceptance_criteria: streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's happy-path test uses a fixed/injected clock instead of DateTime.now(), with no wall-clock polling loop
Test runtime for that test drops from a up-to-5s poll to near-instant

corrections: StreakStateProvider.watch() drives the wait via a Drift .watch() stream plus async restoreIfEmpty, independent of clock source. Injecting a fixed clock fixes the DateTime.now() seed-anchoring (real, valid benefit) but likely won't make the test 'near-instant' as the acceptance criteria states — some bounded wait for the DB stream's first emission would still be needed. Core rule violation stands; recommendation's stated payoff is optimistic.

title: Remove or explicitly justify AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers — dead code duplicating crashlytics_bootstrap.dart's live handlers

recommendation: Delete AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers and its 3 tests, or — if it's meant as a documented fallback for contexts without Crashlytics wired — rename it and add a comment cross-referencing crashlytics_bootstrap.dart so the duplication is intentional and visible rather than accidental drift.

No test exercises a code path unreachable from main.dart's actual bootstrap chain

title: Replace hardcoded English StateError messages in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl with typed error codes
why: EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry a stable code/enum, never a pre-formatted human sentence, because the app ships EN+Hebrew and a raw exception.message/.toString() renders untranslated and un-RTL-shaped. This StateError carries no `.code` field at all — contrast with the codebase's own established pattern for exactly this kind of condition: 4 presentation files (account_actions.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, signup_screen.dart, account_picker_screen.dart) all switch on `GoogleSignInException.code`, never `.message`. The one caller I traced for this specific StateError (sign_in_controller.dart `_extractFirebaseCode`) happens to fall back safely to a translated generic string because its `[plugin/code]` regex doesn't match a StateError's toString() — but that's incidental to that call site's defensive regex, not a guarantee, and the other 3 call sites (deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail flows in features/account) are outside this batch and unverified. The lint meant to catch a raw .toString() reaching UI (no_e_to_string_in_ui) is currently non-functional (custom_lint crashes — baselined), so nothing today would catch a future regression at those sites.
recommendation: Introduce a small typed exception (e.g. NotAuthenticatedException) or a stable error-code enum instead of StateError('...'); have presentation resolve display text via AppLocalizations, matching the .code-switch pattern already used for GoogleSignInException elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: No throw StateError('<english sentence>') remains in firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart; a typed exception without a baked-in human sentence is thrown instead.
Existing 'throws when no user is signed in' tests updated to assert the new exception type.
A grep/test confirms no caller of deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail/sendEmailVerification renders the exception's raw message/toString() in a widget.

corrections: All 4 StateError quotes/lines (103,175,184,198) exact, and the 4-file GoogleSignInException.code-switch pattern is real. But the 'traced caller' claim is wrong: sign_in_controller.dart's resendVerificationEmail (the only caller of sendEmailVerification traced) never calls _extractFirebaseCode at all — it swallows the error into AppLogger.warning with nothing shown to the user, not a regex-fallback to generic text as narrated.

title: Convert HierarchySelection and AdjacentItems to @freezed instead of hand-rolled/missing equality
rule: coding-standards.md:584 — never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes
why: coding-standards.md is explicit: 'hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.' title: Fix ContentTree.parent()'s off-by-one when a leaf precedes its container in source order
rule: Correctness bug (Fowler duplicated-but-inconsistent logic between pass 1 and pass 2)
why: Empirically verified: constructed a 4-level Bavli fixture where the leaf item ('Berakhot 2a:1') appears before its own container ('Berakhot 2a') in the input list, called ContentTree.fromCurricula(...).parent('Berakhot 2a:1'), and got 'Berakhot 2' (the grandparent/daf-level container) instead of the correct immediate parent 'Berakhot 2a'. Root cause: for a leaf, `_ancestorLevels(item)` already returns the PARENT container's own key (that's its documented purpose, and pass 1 at lines 110-121 uses it directly with no further truncation). Pass 2 treats `levels` uniformly as if it were the item's own key and applies a second `.sublist(0, length - 1)` 'walk up one level' step — which, for leaves, walks up an extra level past the true parent. Pass 1 resolves leaves correctly when their container is registered first; pass 2's fallback only fires — with the wrong answer — when a leaf is encountered before its container. ContentTree.parent() currently has zero callers in lib/ (content_hierarchy_screen.dart uses only .children()/.containerFor()), so this is not live-user-visible today, but it is a public, documented, keepAlive-cached API on the exact class whose stated purpose is 'O(1) parent/child/adjacent traversal' — the first feature that calls .parent() for breadcrumb 'up' navigation inherits a silently-wrong result whenever source ordering isn't strictly parent-before-child.
recommendation: In pass 2's leaf branch, use `ancestorLevels` (the value already returned by _ancestorLevels) directly as the parent container key, the same way pass 1 does — do not apply an additional sublist(0, length-1) truncation for leaves.

title: Rewrite ConnectivityGateway's only test — it is tautologically true and hits the real network

title: Cancel or document the leaked DNS-lookup Future in ConnectivityGateway.isOnline on timeout
rule: Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway
why: Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
recommendation: Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
acceptance_criteria: Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout

title: Correct FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime's false claim that the Firestore SDK auto-converts ISO-8601 strings to Timestamp
rule: AG-8-adjacent doc/code truth + Evans (one place for an invariant)

evidence.quote: The Firestore SDK converts ISO-8601 strings into Timestamp objects on write, so this format is safe to use in push documents.
in Firestore Security Rules a `string <= timestamp` comparison is `false`, which would deny EVERY completion create.
timestamp), so a `created_at <= request.time` guard compared a string to request.time and was rejected at the type level —

why: The claim is false — the SDK does not auto-convert a Dart String to a Timestamp. That's exactly why firestore_gateway_impl.dart carries a dedicated `_timestampifyCompletedAt` patch (lines 158-219) that rewrites `completed_at`/`purged_at` from String/DateTime to a real Timestamp AFTER every codec's encode() output runs, and exactly why streak_events' equivalent `created_at <= request.time` rule check was deleted after it denied every write in production. The real fix for a timestamp-compared field lives two layers away from the codec, in a hand-maintained per-field allowlist inside firestore_gateway_impl.dart — a mechanism entity_codec.dart's own 'Responsibilities' docstring never mentions. The next engineer who adds a new entity kind with a `<= request.time` rule, trusts this codec's comment, and skips the gateway patch will reproduce the exact 'permission-denied on every create' incident this codebase has already hit twice (completions, streak_events).
recommendation: Fix the doc comment to state the SDK does NOT auto-convert and cross-reference firestore_gateway_impl.dart's `_timestampifyCompletedAt` as the actual mechanism. Consider moving that per-field patch logic into the codec/EntityCodec layer (or documenting it explicitly in entity_codec.dart's 'Push encoding — SyncWriteFacade territory' note) so the full push contract for a timestamp-compared field lives in one discoverable place instead of three.
acceptance_criteria: encodeDateTime's doc comment no longer claims SDK auto-conversion; it states the true behavior and points to the gateway patch.

rule: Nygard lens (mandatory for this area) — permission-denied at every I/O point; EH-2 typed-exception boundary

evidence.quote: Thrown when a Firestore operation returns PERMISSION_DENIED.

why: _guardPermission (firestore_gateway_impl.dart:1197-1215) is the ONLY code in the app that ever throws FirestorePermissionDeniedException, and it wraps exactly 2 of this gateway's ~30 Firestore I/O methods — fetchPage (524) and fetchChildPage (1051), both reads, both with operation hardcoded to 'read'. None of the ~23 push* (write) methods route through it: pushStreak/pushSettings/pushTrack (288-337) issue raw .set() calls with no try/catch at all, and pushCompletionsBatch (246-285) wraps any commit failure — including permission-denied — as a generic SyncPushException instead. Traced end to end: OutboxProcessor absorbs every push failure internally (never rethrows to any AsyncValue/UI, so this is not a UI-facing bug), but the dedicated permission_denied analytics event in sync_orchestrator.dart (gated on `e is FirestorePermissionDeniedException`) therefore fires only from the pull path and never from an outbox push. The write path's only detector of this failure class is outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters, which pattern-matches raw persisted error text (`lastError.like('%permission-denied%')`) instead of a structured type — a duplicated, Firestore-SDK-wording-dependent re-derivation of the exact fact this exception exists to represent. This repo's own docs (on-device-preflight-cheatsheet.md, bug-hunt-findings-2026-05-31.md) call permission-denied on writes 'a known recurring failure mode in this project,' yet the typed signal for it covers roughly 1 in 15 of the gateway's I/O surface.
recommendation: Route every push*/fetch* method in firestore_gateway_impl.dart through _guardPermission (or an equivalent shared wrapper) with an accurate operation value (read/write/delete) instead of only the 2 fetch methods, so FirestorePermissionDeniedException becomes the single source of truth for 'this failure was permission-denied' on both read and write paths. Then simplify outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters to check a structured signal instead of a LIKE-pattern on free text.
acceptance_criteria: count of _guardPermission( call sites in firestore_gateway_impl.dart increases beyond the current 2 to cover write (push*) methods

title: Deduplicate the copy-pasted cause-suffix toString() snippet across 3 sync exception classes
rule: Fowler duplication (digest lens pass) — Extract Method / Pull Up Field
why: The identical ternary-interpolation snippet is hand-copied into 3 of the 4 exception classes in this directory (SyncPushException uses a 4th, differently-shaped cause format). Each also hand-declares its own nullable cause field because their respective category bases (PermissionException, InternalException) don't carry one — only NetworkException does, per app_exception.dart's hierarchy. If cause-formatting ever needs to change — e.g. to redact a PII-bearing FirebaseException payload before it reaches AppLogger/Crashlytics, a real concern given this app's child-privacy posture — a maintainer has to remember to update 3+ near-identical copies instead of one, and any future 5th leaf exception is likely to copy the same snippet again.

title: Defensively copy SyncPushException.committed so the partial-commit invariant can't be violated by a future caller
rule: Evans lens — invariant enforced in one place, not by caller convention
why: SyncPushException.committed exists specifically so OutboxProcessor can tell which outbox rows genuinely landed before a batch failed, so committed rows are 'never re-pushed or dead-lettered' (per this file's own docstring, H3). That invariant currently holds only because the single production call site remembers to wrap the list in List.unmodifiable(pushed) before throwing — the exception class itself accepts any List<String>, including a live mutable reference, with no internal defensive copy. A future call site (or a test double standing in for one) that passes a growable list it keeps appending to after constructing the exception would silently corrupt the partial-commit accounting this type exists to protect, with no compiler or runtime signal that anything went wrong.
recommendation: Copy defensively inside the constructor (e.g. an initializer that wraps committed in List.unmodifiable(committed)) so the guarantee doesn't depend on every future caller remembering to do it themselves.
acceptance_criteria: a new unit test constructs SyncPushException with a growable list, mutates the original list after construction, and asserts .committed is unaffected

title: Type the bare catch clauses in the merge layer so they stop swallowing Error subtypes

why: Neither catch has an `on <Type>` clause, so both trap Error subtypes (TypeError, RangeError, AssertionError) alongside genuine Exceptions. Per EH-4's stated rationale, that masks real programming bugs introduced by a future edit to these exact files: instead of crashing loudly with a stack trace in dev/QA, a regression degrades silently to a 'sync_learner_profile_merge_row_failed' warning log (site 1) or a silently-emptied schedule days-of-week list inside _encodeSchedule (site 2).

title: Fix LearningLedgerMerger's fallback ULID generator to avoid a permanent same-millisecond collision loss
rule: Nygard: silent, non-self-healing data loss on a manufactured natural-key collision
why: This fallback (only used when a pulled row has no `ulid` — 'legacy data' pre-migration docs, per the file's own comment) is deterministic with zero entropy: two ledger rows completed in the same millisecond with no ulid produce the IDENTICAL synthetic id. LearningLedgerDao dedups on ulid via INSERT OR IGNORE, so the second row is silently dropped — permanently, since a retry regenerates the same colliding id every time (unlike the rest of this merge layer's failures, which self-heal on the next pull because the underlying condition changes). A bulk-mark flow (bulk_mark_screen.dart is a named churn hotspot) writing several legacy-shaped completions together is a plausible trigger.
recommendation: Add entropy to the fallback id (e.g. an index-within-batch or random suffix instead of a constant zero-padded tail), or skip rows with no ulid and no way to disambiguate instead of manufacturing a collidable one.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: merge two distinct legacy (no-ulid) rows sharing the same completed_at millisecond — assert both are inserted, not deduplicated into one.

corrections: The bulk_mark_screen.dart trigger example is unsupported: local ledger writes always assign a real ULID via newUlid(now) (learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:107,174), so bulk-marking today cannot produce a no-ulid row. Only genuine pre-ULID-migration Firestore docs can reach the _makeUlid fallback; the core collision mechanism itself is confirmed correct.

      if (reset != null) await reset();

rule: SM-6 lazy-resolver consistency / Nygard-lens: stale capture across DB swap
why: Every other volatile build-time dependency in this same constructor call (gateway, merge router, outbox DAO, identity status) is deliberately passed as a lazy `() => ref.read(...)` resolver specifically — per the inline comments at lines 136-137, 161-163 — 'so a DB swap (multi-account flow) is picked up without rebuilding the orchestrator singleton.' outboxProcessor is the one exception: it's read once (line 129) and stored as a plain value field. outboxProcessorProvider (outbox_providers.dart) watches userDatabaseProvider and rebuilds on a DB swap; database_provider.dart confirms userDatabaseProvider swaps via the independently-mutable accountDbFileNameProvider, decoupled from authStateProvider (the only thing syncOrchestratorProvider itself watches). If a DB swap can occur without authStateProvider's watched value also changing in the same tick, the orchestrator keeps draining through an OutboxProcessor bound to the pre-swap, superseded UserDatabase/outboxDao while its other lazily-resolved collaborators (gateway, merge router) may already be pointing at the new account — a split-identity state. Confirming this needs tracing whether the app's account-switch flow (account_actions.dart) can complete a DB swap before authStateProvider's emitted value settles to the new account.
recommendation: Change the outboxProcessor parameter to a lazy `resolveOutboxProcessor: () => ref.read(outboxProcessorProvider)` resolver, matching resolveGateway/resolveMergeRouter/resolveOutboxDao, so it can't go stale relative to its siblings.
acceptance_criteria: syncOrchestratorProvider resolves outboxProcessor via a lazy resolver rather than a captured value.

Regression/integration test: trigger a userDatabaseProvider swap while syncOrchestratorProvider stays alive (authState unchanged) and assert the next drain operates against the new outboxDao's pending rows, not the pre-swap instance.

why: Both tests tap a curriculum row and assert only that `tester.takeException()` is non-null — that passes for any exception at all, including an unrelated build error introduced by a future regression, not specifically the intended 'no AutoRouter in the test tree' push failure. hierarchy_navigation_test.dart also pre-builds elaborate filterByLevel mocks for three deeper drill levels (Berachos, Perek 1, Mishna 1) that are never exercised because the test ends at the very first tap — dead setup code that makes the test look far more thorough than it is. title: Merge the duplicate TextCacheRepository and TextDisplayScreen test files produced by parallel coverage-wave commits

// Extra coverage for TextCacheRepository — exercises the text_cache hit path,
// L1 widget tests for TextDisplayScreen — the text reader (67.5% coverage focus)

Keep text_display_screen_l1_test.dart as primary, fold any assertion unique to text_display_screen_test.dart (e.g. the AppBar-shows-sefariaRef case) into it, then delete the old file. title: Fix the tautological 'Gematriya correctness' test in text_display_screen_deep_l1_test.dart to call the real Gematriya.forNumber
rule: TQ-8 (tautological test — asserts what a local copy returns, not the production code)

evidence.quote: // avoid importing a lib/ class that could pull in unwanted transitive deps.

why: The test name promises to verify Gematriya.forNumber's halachically-significant 15/16 substitution (טו/טז instead of spelling the divine name), but it never calls Gematriya.forNumber — it calls a private `_gematriya()` helper in the same test file that hand-copies the lookup table as a literal Dart map. The stated reason ('avoid importing a lib/ class that could pull in unwanted transitive deps') does not hold: lib/core/utils/gematriya.dart is a zero-import, private-constructor pure-static class, and 20+ other tests in this very file already import lib/ classes freely (TutorPermissions, ResolvedSession, MarkLiveCompletionUseCase). If Gematriya.forNumber were changed or broken, this test would keep passing because it only checks the copied table against itself. Real protection for the underlying rule does exist elsewhere — test/core/utils/gematriya_test.dart and gematriya_ts6_test.dart call the real class, and this same file's C1/C2 tests exercise Gematriya.forNumber indirectly through widget rendering — so the concrete risk today is low, but this specific 'Direct assertion for completeness' test contributes zero verification while reading as if it does.
recommendation: Delete the local _gematriya helper and its hardcoded table; import package:learning_tracker/core/utils/gematriya.dart and call Gematriya.forNumber directly in the assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Test calls Gematriya.forNumber(15)/(16) etc. directly; temporarily corrupting Gematriya's 15/16 special-case in lib/ makes this specific test fail.

title: Replace tautological ConstrainedBox-ancestor check in r2_panel_leaf_crumb_ellipsis_test.dart with a real width-bound assertion
why: Empirically verified via mutation testing: with the real fix in place, `flutter test` passes 4/4. Reverting hierarchy_selection_panel.dart's leaf-crumb Text to a bare `Text(label)` (no overflow/maxLines/ConstrainedBox) makes the suite RED as expected — but reverting only the `ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: maxLeafCrumbWidth)` wrapper while leaving `overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis, maxLines: 1, softWrap: false` on the Text keeps all 4 cases GREEN. Instrumenting the finder shows why: it matches TextButton's own internal minimum-tap-target box (`ConstrainedBox(64.0<=w<=Infinity, 40.0<=h<=Infinity)`), not the fix's width cap. So a future regression that removes the actual width bound — exactly the failure mode the test's own `reason:` string names ("leaf crumb must be width-capped so ellipsis engages") — would ship undetected even though this file is tagged as the regression test for that bug.
recommendation: Assert on the rendered geometry instead of "any ConstrainedBox exists": either read the leaf Text's `RenderBox` size via `tester.getSize(find.byWidget(leaf))` and assert its width is bounded (e.g. <= panel width), or use `find.ancestor(matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w is ConstrainedBox && w.constraints.maxWidth < double.infinity))` so TextButton's own unrelated min-size box can't satisfy the finder.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running the test against a widget with the ConstrainedBox width-cap stripped (overflow/maxLines left in place) fails RED on the updated assertion.
All 4 parametrized LTR/RTL x scale cases stay GREEN with the real fix in place.

title: Fix Makefile check 15's awk logic — it structurally can never flag a cross-feature deep import
area: tooling/Makefile (Rule 2 checker) — surfaced while verifying content_browsing layering

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'
awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}';

why: match($0, ...) scans the whole `path:line:content` string and returns the FIRST `features/X/` match — which is always inside the file-path prefix, identical to what match($1, ...) already extracted from the path alone. So a[1] and b[1] are always equal and `if(a[1] != b[1])` never fires, regardless of input. Verified by running the exact pipeline against the live tree: it returns 0 lines. Yet real cross-feature deep imports exist and bypass their feature's providers.dart barrel — e.g. lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/widgets/hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:14 imports 'package:learning_tracker/features/tracks/setup/domain/entities/add_track_result.dart' directly, and a broader scan turned up 40+ more instances just under lib/features/tracks/. This is a different, more severe problem than the already-documented 'checks 14-15 are warn-only' backlog: check 14 (Rule 1) is warn-only but does enumerate its ~32 known edges every run; check 15 (Rule 2) has never printed a single violation and would stay silent even on a brand-new cross-feature deep import introduced today, so Rule 2 currently has zero live detection, not merely non-blocking detection.
recommendation: Fix the second match() to search only the substring after the file path's own feature segment (e.g. split $1 out of $0 first, or anchor the second regex to the import-statement portion of the line only), then re-run and baseline the newly-real violation list the same way check 14 already documents its known edges.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15 prints hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:14 (and other live cross-feature deep imports) as WARN output on the current tree.

A synthetic fixture file with a deliberate cross-feature deep import (not via providers.dart) makes check 15's grep pipeline produce non-empty output; a fixture using only same-feature or providers.dart-barrel imports keeps it silent.

title: Guard ref.watch/ref.read after in-flight awaits in dashboard_providers.dart (SM-4)
why: dashboardTrackCompletionPercentage, dashboardCompletionPercentage, stripStockMilestonesEffect, and dashboardPaceStatus each call ref.watch/ref.read after an earlier await (a Drift DB read) with no ref.mounted check in between. If any of these autoDispose family providers loses its last listener while that DB read is still in flight — e.g. the user swipes the active-tracks carousel past a card or leaves the dashboard mid-load — the later ref call throws UnmountedRefException, an uncaught exception inside the async provider body. The same file's dashboardChildNextReward provider (line 343) already guards this exact hazard with `if (!ref.mounted) return null;`, proving the team knows the failure mode; it just isn't applied consistently.
recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return <default>;` immediately after the await that precedes the later ref access in each of the four functions, mirroring the existing guard in dashboardChildNextReward.
acceptance_criteria: A targeted test that disposes the ProviderContainer (or drops the last listener) mid-await for each of the four providers confirms no UnmountedRefException escapes.
A grep/lint check for 'ref.watch|ref.read after await without a preceding ref.mounted guard' is added to make audit or riverpod_lint config.

title: Inject LocalDayClock into ParentDashboardAggregator instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
why: compute({DateTime? now}) documents now as 'pass explicitly for testability', and every other metric (pace, engagement, recent-completions window) honors it — but the streak sub-computation always builds StreakStateProvider with a hardcoded SystemLocalDayClock(), which reads real DateTime.now() regardless of the now argument. The accompanying test cannot control this and is forced to call real DateTime.now() to seed matching streak_events (quoted comment at lines 119-121 explains exactly why), making that test a genuine wall-clock dependency and leaving a live day-boundary race: if the wall clock ticks past local midnight between the caller choosing now and StreakStateProvider's internal clock read, currentStreak/maxStreak reflect a different 'today' than the rest of the ParentDashboardData snapshot.
recommendation: Accept an optional LocalDayClock clock constructor parameter (default const SystemLocalDayClock()), pass it into StreakStateProvider, and derive it from the aggregator's own now so compute(now: ...) fully determines the snapshot including streak.
acceptance_criteria: A new unit test overrides the injected clock (not real DateTime.now()) and asserts currentStreak/maxStreak for a fixed 'today', replacing the wall-clock seeding at parent_dashboard_aggregator_compute_test.dart:118-122.

title: Log RewardMilestoneService.getAllMilestones/getAllUnlocks JSON-decode failures instead of silently returning an empty list that can later overwrite cloud data

title: Fix the Makefile check-15 awk pipeline so cross-feature deep-import detection can actually fire
rule: Rule 0 / Rule 2 / AG-11 (a standard ships with a deterministic checker; checker failures print file:line and exit non-zero -- a check that structurally cannot fire is a broken guardrail)

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

why: $1 (awk field 1, the file path column) and $0 (the whole grep output line, which starts with that same file path) are both matched against the identical regex `features/([^/]+)/` -- since the file's own path is always the leftmost occurrence of that pattern in $0 too, `a[1]` and `b[1]` are always extracted from the SAME text (the importing file's own feature folder), so `a[1] != b[1]` can never be true and the check prints nothing, always, regardless of what's actually imported. I reproduced the exact pipeline directly: the grep -P pre-filter stage alone finds 70+ candidate cross-feature import lines (including at least 10 genuine features/{dashboard,learning,notifications,sync,content_browsing}/** files deep-importing into features/gamification/**), but piping through the full check-15 awk command yields exactly 0 output lines. Unlike check 14 (which lists its ~32-edge backlog so it's at least visible for future cleanup), check 15 gives zero visibility into the Rule 2 backlog size today, and -- more importantly -- will never flag a brand-new cross-feature deep import added by any future change, even once the check is flipped from warn-only to enforcing.
recommendation: Fix the awk script to compare the importing file's feature folder against the IMPORTED path's feature folder specifically (e.g. split $1 and the import-statement portion of $0 separately, or use two distinct match targets), then re-run make audit and confirm it lists the real backlog the way check 14 does.
acceptance_criteria: Running the check-15 pipeline against the current tree (unchanged) prints the real cross-feature deep-import edges instead of nothing

title: Wrap LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl's ledger insert and outbox enqueue in one transaction

recommendation: Move the outbox enqueue for recordCompletion inside the same transaction as the ledger insert (or into one atomic Drift batch, as CompletionWriter does); for recordCompletionsBatch, move the per-item enqueueLedgerEntry calls inside the existing transaction block instead of running them afterward in a separate loop.

title: Wrap SacredWindowEntries clear+insert in one transaction (DB-2)
why: The table is briefly empty between clearAll() completing and insertAll() starting; neither call is awaited by any caller and neither is wrapped in a transaction. invalidate()'s own separate unawaited clearAll() (line 50) can also interleave with _persistToDb()'s clear-then-insert pair (line 167) in either order. The class's own doc says this cache exists so 'background notification-fire-time checks can read them on cold-start without the Flutter engine' -- a background read landing in the empty gap, or after invalidate() wins a race against a slower insertAll(), sees no Sacred Time windows and could fail to suppress a notification during Shabbos/Yom Tov, the entire point of DNI-367. Confirming the full consequence requires reading the background notification-fire-time isolate handler, which is outside this batch.
recommendation: Wrap clear+insert in one db.transaction(...) and await it from both invalidate() and _persistToDb(), or add an explicit generation-counter guard so a stale clear can't stomp a newer insert.
acceptance_criteria: A DAO-level test that races invalidate() against a concurrent _persistToDb() cycle never observes SacredWindowEntries transition through an empty state once a non-empty write has committed.

title: Use a clock-skew-safe timestamp, not client clock, for notification_settings updated_at LWW field
why: This client-computed timestamp becomes the payload's updated_at field pushed via enqueueNotificationSettings; core/sync/merge/notification_settings_merger.dart (outside this batch) parses remote['updated_at'] to arbitrate LWW. If two devices' clocks disagree, the device with the faster/wrong clock can push a stale settings change that looks 'newer' and wins over a genuinely newer change made on a correctly-clocked device, silently reverting the user's real edit with no error surfaced anywhere. Confirming the full blast radius requires reading the outbox-drain write path (outside this batch) to see whether it overwrites this field with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() before commit.
recommendation: Confirm whether the write path already substitutes a server timestamp before commit; if not, do so, or route the push side through the same clock-skew arbitration MergeStore.remoteIsNewer already implements for the pull side.
acceptance_criteria: A sync test with an artificially-skewed local clock demonstrates the genuinely later settings write wins regardless of which device has the faster clock.

corrections: DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() confirmed to be raw SystemLocalDayClock (core/utils/date_utils.dart:15-19) — genuinely uncorrected client clock, strengthening the claim.

title: Test the real _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud signature logic, not a hand-copied reimplementation
why: _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud's M2 no-op-skip logic (skip pushing when the settings signature hasn't changed, to avoid bumping updated_at and clobbering a newer remote under LWW -- the exact mechanism the client-clock finding depends on) is a private function, so G1-G4 reimplement its string format by hand in the test file instead of exercising it. If a future edit to the real signature-building code drops a field or changes the separator, breaking the no-op-skip contract, G1-G4 keep passing because they never call the real function.
recommendation: Extract the signature-building into an internal @visibleForTesting function the tests can call directly, or drive it end-to-end via notificationSettingsCloudSyncEffectProvider with a fake outbox facade asserting enqueue is/isn't called across setting changes.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation check confirms G1-G4 (or their replacement) fail when a field is removed from the real signature-building code in notification_providers.dart.

title: Convert ReminderPreferences to @freezed instead of hand-rolled ==/hashCode/copyWith
why: Matches the coding standard's explicit rule to never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes. The 7 fields are consistent between == and hashCode today, but every future field addition is a manual 3-way sync across the constructor, ==, hashCode and copyWith -- an easy place to introduce a silent equality bug (a field present in the constructor but missed in == makes two logically-different instances compare equal).
recommendation: Convert to @freezed class ReminderPreferences with _$ReminderPreferences.

recommendation: Add `reminderSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` and `streakAlertSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` to both builders, matching notifications_screen_l1_test.dart's pattern, so no real UserDatabase/scheduler chain is ever constructed in these widget tests.

title: Stop relying on find.byKey(...).last for time-row lookups in notifications_screen_l1_test.dart and notifications_screen_test.dart
why: _SettingsTimeRow (learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen.dart:306, `return ListTile(key: key, ...)`) forwards its own key onto the inner ListTile it builds, so Key('reminder_time')/Key('streak_alert_time') each match 2 elements in the tree. All 8 sites paper over that with `.last`, trusting find.byKey's traversal order to put the ListTile after its wrapper -- an implementation detail, not a documented Flutter API contract -- while the very same file already uses a robust, order-independent alternative for the Switch rows (e.g. l1_test.dart:218-220, `find.descendant(of: reminderRow, matching: find.byType(Switch))`). If the match order ever flipped, `.last` would silently resolve to the wrapper widget and the ensuing `tester.widget<ListTile>(...)` cast would throw, breaking otherwise-unrelated tests with a confusing error.
recommendation: Match the ListTile the same way the Switch rows already do -- e.g. `find.widgetWithText(ListTile, l10n.notifReminderTime)` or, on the production side, stop forwarding `key` to the inner ListTile in _SettingsTimeRow and instead expose a distinct key for it -- so the finder resolves to exactly one widget without depending on registration order.

title: Guard ref.mounted after awaits in PinFlowController._handleSetup/_handleChange/_handleVerify (SM-4)
why: PinFlowController is @Riverpod(keepAlive: true), so it survives normal widget disposal, but keepAlive doesn't prevent explicit container disposal (app teardown, ref.invalidate, hot-restart, or a route pop mid-flight) while a bcrypt verify/hash is in flight — bcrypt is deliberately slow, widening this window. Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException from a post-await `state = ...` write if the container is gone by then. None of the 4 awaited PinService call sites (_handleSetup confirm-save, _handleChange verifyCurrent and confirm-save, _handleVerify) check ref.mounted first, and none of the 628 lines in pin_flow_controller_test.dart dispose the container between firing an async PIN action and that action resolving — every async test either awaits full completion or uses a never-resolving Future, so this path is never exercised. Runtime confirmation needs a test that disposes mid-await and checks the outcome is clean rather than an uncaught exception.
recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after each of the 4 awaited PinService calls, before the subsequent state write. Add a regression test that disposes the container after the 4th digit triggers the async handler but before the pending PinService future resolves.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 4 sites has a ref.mounted guard after its await.
A new test disposes mid-flight and passes without an uncaught UnmountedRefException.

corrections: PinFlowChangeRoute/PinFlowVerifyRoute (covering _handleChange's 2 sites and _handleVerify's 1 site) are registered in app_router.dart but never pushed anywhere in lib/ (confirmed via grep) — only PinFlowSetupRoute is live. why: Per SM-4 (and the digest's own note that Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException), every `await` in a Notifier method must be followed by a `ref.mounted` check before touching `state`. title: Guard ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile's cloud-sync push the same way create/update/ensureDefaultProfile do
why: createProfile, updateProfile, and ensureDefaultProfile all wrap their `_syncEngine?.push*` call in try/catch with an explicit 'offline-first, cloud push is non-fatal' comment. deleteProfile does not: `await _syncEngine?.deleteLearnerProfile(id)` runs bare, after the local cascade-delete transaction has already committed across ~12 tables. Both push and delete enqueue through the same outbox `_enqueue` mechanism (a local Drift insert), so they carry the same theoretical failure mode (e.g. disk-full, DB-locked). If that insert throws, the whole deleteProfile Future rejects even though the profile is already gone locally — and neither of deleteProfile's two callers in this batch (profile_edit_delete_actions.dart's deleteProfileFlow, profile_picker_screen.dart's _showDeleteDialog) catch it either, so the exception surfaces as an unhandled error in a button's onPressed handler while the delete has, in fact, already succeeded — contradicting the offline-first invariant this same file documents for every other mutation.
recommendation: Wrap `await _syncEngine?.deleteLearnerProfile(id)` in the same non-fatal try/catch (with logging per the previous finding) used by createProfile/updateProfile/ensureDefaultProfile.
acceptance_criteria: deleteProfile's sync call is wrapped in try/catch matching its siblings, with a logged, non-fatal failure

title: Fix Makefile check-15 cross-feature-import grep — it can structurally never detect a violation
rule: Rule 2 (cross-feature deep imports) / Rule 0 checker correctness / AG-11

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

why: match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b) re-scans the WHOLE line (path:linenum:import-text) for the leftmost 'features/X/' substring, which is always inside the file-path field that a[1] already captured — so b[1] is always identical to a[1] and the check can never print a WARN, no matter how many real cross-feature deep imports exist. I reproduced the exact pipeline against a real offending line and confirmed a[1]=b[1]='progress' even though the import target feature is 'content_browsing'. As a direct, concrete consequence, siyumim_grouped_view.dart:10 deep-imports content_browsing's provider file instead of the (currently empty) content_browsing.dart barrel, and make audit reports check 15 as clean regardless. The correctly-written custom_lint equivalent (no_feature_cross_import, ERROR severity) would catch this, but that tool currently crashes on every run — so both enforcement layers for Rule 2 are simultaneously non-functional, for two unrelated reasons, and nobody would know new violations are accumulating.
recommendation: Rewrite the awk to isolate the imported feature name from the import-URI field only (not re-scan $0), add a Makefile-test fixture proving check 15 fires on a synthetic cross-feature deep import and stays silent on a same-feature one, then re-run make audit to see and triage the real (likely multi-file) backlog this uncovers across lib/features/.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture cross-feature deep import makes check 15 print a WARN; a same-feature deep import does not.
make audit re-run after the fix lists siyumim_grouped_view.dart:10 under check 15.
Decision recorded on whether the newly-surfaced backlog gets baselined (like the 32 Rule-1 edges) or fixed before check 15 can be promoted off warn-only.

title: Stop keying GoalEntity.firestoreId on mutable targetPercent — every goal-percent edit orphans a Firestore document instead of updating it
rule: Evans invariant (aggregate identity must be stable across normal mutation); adjacent to the FB family's stable-natural-key principle

evidence.quote: test('two goals with different createdAt have different firestoreIds', () {

why: firestoreId = curriculumId + '_' + targetPercent.toStringAsFixed(1) + '_' + createdAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch. updateGoal preserves createdAt but allows targetPercent to change, so any 'adjust my goal target %' edit (a routine, expected user action) computes a DIFFERENT firestoreId and _syncGoal pushes a brand-new Firestore document instead of updating the original — the original document is never touched again and deleteGoal only ever removes the CURRENT firestoreId's doc, so the old one is orphaned forever. GoalMerger happens to key its LWW arbitration by track_id rather than firestoreId, so the local state pulled on other devices generally self-heals to the latest edit — but Firestore itself accumulates one permanent garbage document per percent-edit for the life of the account, silently inflating every future full pull of that profile's goals collection. The test suite tests firestoreId's format exhaustively (contains curriculumId / contains targetPercent / contains createdAt, in TWO separate near-duplicate files) and even exercises the exact repro (create at 50.0, update to 75.0) but never asserts the one invariant that matters: the id must stay the same across that edit.
recommendation: Derive firestoreId only from fields that cannot change through updateGoal (drop targetPercent from the id, or key on the DB row id / trackId+curriculumId+createdAt) so an update always resolves to the same document.
acceptance_criteria: GoalEntity.firestoreId no longer includes targetPercent (or any other field updateGoal can change).
New regression test: create a goal, call updateGoal changing only targetPercent, and assert the pushed sync payload's id/firestoreId is identical to the create call's.

title: Add a profileId ownership check to GoalRepositoryImpl.updateGoal/deleteGoal and unify its profileId source

why: getGoals() filters by the constructor-injected _profileId field, but createGoal takes its own explicit profileId parameter that is never cross-checked against _profileId — the interface lets a caller create a goal 'for' a different profile than the repository instance represents, which would then be invisible to that same instance's getGoals(). Independently, updateGoal and deleteGoal load the existing row by bare goalId and mutate/delete it with no ownership check at all — updateGoal even copies existing.profileId straight back into the write (line-133, not separately confirmed) without ever comparing it to _profileId. None of this is proven to be hit by today's UI (all current call sites happen to pass matching profileIds), but the repository adds zero defense-in-depth on top of the DAO layer (which itself does not scope goalDao.updateGoal/deleteGoal/getGoalById by profile) — the next screen or bug that supplies a mismatched id/profileId pair silently edits or deletes another profile's goal.
recommendation: Pick one source of truth for 'which profile owns this repository instance' and have updateGoal/deleteGoal verify existing.profileId against it before mutating, throwing a typed error on mismatch.

title: Resolve the ambiguous stageId/stageOrder dual-interpretation in SchedulerCompletionRepositoryImpl.resolveStageOrder
rule: Evans lens — a single field pattern-matched against two overlapping ID spaces with no way to tell them apart

evidence.quote:
final stageOrderMap = {for (final s in stages) s.id: s.stageOrder};
    final knownStageOrders = {for (final s in stages) s.stageOrder};

why: The comment says newer completion rows store a stage's stageOrder in c.stageId while older rows store the stage's DB id; resolveStageOrder tries to guess which format a given row used by checking 'does rawStageId match some CURRENT stage's stageOrder' first. Stage id (a table-wide autoincrement) and stageOrder (a small 1..N per-curriculum ordinal) share the same small-integer space, especially for the first curriculum/stages ever created in a fresh install or test DB (id and stageOrder can be identical by coincidence, e.g. 1,2,3). When they collide, an OLD-format row that really means 'stage id 3' gets misread as 'stageOrder 3' and silently resolves to the wrong stage — which would misreport a chazara/review stage as complete (or vice versa) with no error. I have not constructed a concrete seed scenario proving the collision fires against real data (id values grow globally across curricula, so the window narrows over an install's lifetime), so this is reported as SUSPECTED, not CONFIRMED — a runtime/unit test seeding a stage whose id equals a different stage's stageOrder plus an old-format completion would confirm or rule it out.
recommendation: Give completion rows an explicit format marker (or normalize all stored stageId values to stageOrder in a one-time migration) instead of guessing per-row from an ambiguous value.
acceptance_criteria: A targeted unit test seeds two stages where one stage's DB id equals another (or the same) stage's stageOrder, adds an old-format completion using the id, and asserts resolveStageOrder resolves to the correct stage rather than the coincidentally-matching one.
If the test confirms a collision, resolveStageOrder no longer disambiguates by value coincidence (explicit format tag, or a completed one-time backfill removes the dual-format need).

title: Normalize config.currentDate before delay-stage due-date arithmetic in SchedulerEngine
why: config.currentDate flows in unnormalized: allDailyTasksProvider sets `now = ref.watch(clockProvider)` (a raw timestamp with time-of-day) and _buildFreshPlan passes it straight through generator.generateAll(activeCurricula, now, ...) -> ScheduleConfig(currentDate: date). previousCompletedAt also carries a real time-of-day (completion timestamps are never normalized — confirmed via completion_writer.dart). Duration.inDays truncates toward zero, so when the true calendar-day gap is exactly 1 day but the elapsed wall-clock time is <24h (e.g. item completed at 20:00 five days ago, now it's 02:00 the next calendar day — only 6h elapsed), daysUntilDue computes 0 instead of -1: a chazara item that is genuinely 1+ calendar days overdue is shown in 'due today' (scheduledTasks) instead of 'overdue' (overdueTasks), silently under-reporting overdue-ness by up to a day. recommendation: Normalize both previousCompletedAt/currentCompletedAt and config.currentDate to calendar-date-only (e.g. via DateUtils.extractLocalDate) before computing daysUntilDue in _processDelayStage, matching the pattern already used in _buildProjectionTasks.
acceptance_criteria: New unit test: a delay-stage item whose previous-stage completedAt time-of-day is later than the current query's time-of-day, with a true 1-calendar-day gap, asserts the task lands in overdueTasks (not scheduledTasks).

title: Guard SkippedTasks.build()'s fire-and-forget prefs load with ref.mounted
why: build() kicks off an un-awaited async side effect (SM-2 forbids side effects in build). _loadFromPrefs() then does `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` and further awaits before writing `state = ...` twice, with no `ref.mounted` check (SM-4) anywhere in the method. If the provider is disposed (e.g. the user navigates off the Scheduler screen quickly) before the load resolves, the post-await `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException — which the surrounding try/catch swallows and logs via `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'Failed to load skipped tasks', ...)`, i.e. a routine dispose race gets misreported as a genuine load failure in production logs/Crashlytics breadcrumbs, obscuring real failures of the same code path.
recommendation: Check `ref.mounted` immediately before each `state = ...` assignment in _loadFromPrefs, and return early (without logging) when unmounted, matching Riverpod 3's documented SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

recommendation: Wrap the DB write in try/catch with an AppLogger.error call and user-facing feedback on failure; check `context.mounted` (or equivalent) before the `ref.invalidate` call, matching the guard already present for the SnackBar.

Two near-identical local-date helpers in the same file is exactly the kind of drift that produced the R4-1 class of bugs this feature has repeatedly had to fix — a future edit to one 'extract local date' helper (e.g. a DST or leap-second fix) won't automatically apply to the other.
recommendation: Delete _localDateOnly and call DateUtils.extractLocalDate at its two call sites instead.
acceptance_criteria: _localDateOnly is removed from scheduler_providers.dart; its call sites use DateUtils.extractLocalDate.

title: Migrate scheduler-adjacent tests off the deprecated LearningProgramRepository.instance singleton
why: This static singleton is exactly the 'global/static mutable singleton' SM-7 prohibits, and it has zero production (lib/) call sites — but 30+ test files across the suite (test/core/services/*, test/story_acceptance/*, test/features/tracks/*, test/features/onboarding/*, etc.) construct their fixtures via `LearningProgramRepository.instance` instead of overriding `learningProgramRepositoryProvider`. Because `test/` and `lib/` share one Dart package, Dart's default `deprecated_member_use` lint does not fire for same-package usage (only `deprecated_member_use_from_same_package` would, and it isn't enabled) — which is exactly why `flutter analyze: No issues found` coexists with 30+ live uses of a member explicitly marked for removal. The singleton can never actually be deleted while this fan-out exists, and every test using it is verifying against a construction path the app itself no longer uses.
recommendation: Migrate test fixtures to override learningProgramRepositoryProvider via ProviderContainer overrides instead of reading the singleton directly; once the fan-out is gone, delete the singleton entirely.
acceptance_criteria: New test code does not introduce further LearningProgramRepository.instance call sites.
Existing call sites tracked for migration (e.g. a DNI ticket) with a path to eventual deletion of the singleton.

corrections: Actual scope is 12 test files with 34 real .instance construction call sites, not '30+ test files' as stated — the finding conflated call-site count with file count. Substance unaffected.

title: Fix make audit check 15/15's awk logic — it can never detect a cross-feature deep import
rule: Rule 2 (no cross-feature deep imports) / Rule 0 (checker must actually detect violations)
area: Makefile `make audit` tooling (discovered via a features/scheduler test import)
why: match($0, ...) scans the WHOLE grep -rn output line (`path:line:content`), so it always matches the leftmost `features/<X>/` substring — which is the FILE's own path segment — identical to what match($1, ...) already captured. b[1] therefore always equals a[1] and `if(a[1] != b[1])` can mathematically never be true. Verified with an isolated repro piping the real scheduler_engine.dart grep-rn line through the exact awk expression: both captures resolve to 'scheduler', differ=0. Consequence: check 15/15 has never printed a single violation on any `make audit` run regardless of how many real cross-feature deep imports exist in lib/features/ — it currently misses both lib/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine.dart:11 and test/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart:12, which both import features/tracks/stages/domain/models/schedule_type.dart directly instead of via a tracks.dart barrel. `make audit`'s 'PASSED — all 22 greps clean' banner therefore gives false assurance specifically for Rule 2: an unbounded amount of cross-feature coupling could accumulate with zero signal to any developer or CI run.
recommendation: Rewrite the awk step to derive b[1] from the import-statement text only (e.g. strip the `path:line:` prefix with a field split on the first two colons before matching, or match specifically on `package:learning_tracker/features/([^/]+)/`), and add a regression fixture (a deliberately cross-feature-importing line) that the check must catch so this can't silently regress again.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture cross-feature import line makes `make audit` check 15/15 print a WARN; a test/CI step proves the check fails closed when the fixture is present.

Re-run `make audit` after the fix and triage the resulting real violation list, starting with scheduler_engine.dart:11 and scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart:12 — route through the tracks.dart barrel or add to a documented baseline.

title: Replace fixed Future.delayed sleeps with a deterministic await in scheduler provider tests
rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests, no timing-based synchronization) / Fowler flaky-test smell
why: Every one of these sites follows the same pattern: `c.listen(skippedTasksProvider, (_, __) {})` then a hardcoded 100-200ms sleep, hoping SkippedTasks._loadFromPrefs() (fired via `unawaited()` inside build()) finished first — instead of awaiting the load itself, because the notifier exposes no future to await. Under a loaded CI runner or slower SharedPreferences-mock resolution the guess can be wrong: assertions then run against the stale initial `{}` state, or (in the several tests that call `.skip()`/`.undoSkip()` immediately after the sleep) a late-resolving `_loadFromPrefs()` can overwrite `state` with old prefs data right after the test's own mutation, silently clobbering it. The result is an intermittent, hard-to-reproduce CI failure with no diagnostic pointing at the real cause, plus 3+ seconds of pure sleep time paid on every run across these 4 files.
recommendation: Give SkippedTasks a way to be awaited deterministically (e.g. an internal `Future<void>` the notifier tracks that a test helper can await via `container.read(...notifier).debugReadyForTest`), or restructure as an AsyncNotifier so tests can `await container.read(skippedTasksProvider.future)`. Replace all fixed-delay call sites with that await.
acceptance_criteria: No `Future<void>.delayed` remains in test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/*.dart used purely to wait for provider initialization.
A test that artificially slows the fake SharedPreferences resolution (e.g. via a delayed Future in the mock) still passes, proving synchronization is no longer time-based.

title: Remove UserProfileHeaderCard's redundant _user field and de-duplicate/select-narrow the active-profile lookup
why: _UserProfileHeaderCardState is a ConsumerStatefulWidget solely to hold _user, which initState/didUpdateWidget always sets to exactly widget.user -- functionally identical to reading widget.user directly, which would let this be a plain ConsumerWidget. Separately, the 3-line 'resolve active profile from the profile-list stream' expression (ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider) + ref.watch(profileListStreamProvider) + .where(...).firstOrNull) is copy-pasted verbatim between this build method (lines 112-119) and _LocalBornProfileRow.build (lines 346-350), and neither uses `.select()` to narrow the read to just the active profile -- both widgets rebuild on any change to the full profile list, not just the active one.
recommendation: Delete _user/initState/didUpdateWidget and convert to ConsumerWidget; extract the active-profile lookup into one shared helper/derived provider (ideally using .select) used by both build methods.
acceptance_criteria: user_profile_header_card_l1_test.dart passes unchanged after the refactor.

corrections: Minor: second evidence line cited as 112 is actually 113 (activeProfileId line); the 346 citation is exact. 'Copy-pasted verbatim' slightly overstates since the state version has an extra 'widget.activeProfile ??' prefix, but the duplicated core lookup logic is real.

Today's margins (e.g. a 30s buffer under the 60s 'just now' cliff) make an actual flake unlikely, but the suite is non-deterministic by construction and the gap between test-now and widget-build-now is unbounded on a loaded/slow CI runner.

Also, DateTimeFactory.nowLocal() is gated by the global currentLocalDayClock (set via useLocalDayClock()), not by the Riverpod localDayClockProvider — overriding the latter alone would not fix this widget's read.

title: outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider mutates DAO state and fires a network re-enqueue from inside its Provider build function
why: The code directly inside `Provider<OutboxSyncWriteFacade?>((ref) {...})` mutates pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and unawaited-fires reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId) unconditionally on every build. This provider watches authStateProvider, activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider, userDatabaseProvider, activeProfileIdProvider, and localDayClockProvider -- any of which changing (e.g. every profile switch in this multi-child app) reruns build and refires the recovery scan, which its own D14 comment says is meant to run once. SM-2 exists precisely because 'side effects in build race and get skipped or duplicated on rebuild' -- here they duplicate on every rebuild instead of running once.
recommendation: Move syncSink wiring and the one-time ledger-recovery call out of build into a ref.listen/onDispose pairing or an explicit one-shot recovery triggered on cloud-conversion, leaving build to only construct and return the facade.
acceptance_criteria: riverpod_lint/custom_lint rule flagging DAO field mutation or unawaited async calls directly inside a Provider build body (SM-2 Enforce backstop).
Regression test with a spy DAO asserting reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows is invoked at most once per profile per session, not once per rebuild (simulate two profile switches).

corrections: The finding's 'why' misquotes sync_providers.dart:175's own comment (actual text: 'Idempotent + fire-and-forget so it never blocks the UI', not 'meant to run once'). points_balance_dao.dart:559-567's doc comment on reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows explicitly states it is idempotent and should be 'call[ed] right after wiring syncSink (cloud session start / profile switch)' — refiring on every profile switch is the designed behavior, not the duplication bug SM-2 warns about. The bare side-effect-in-build pattern smell is still real, but there is no demonstrated concrete cost, so this is hygiene not design debt.

title: onEnqueueDrain closures in sync_providers.dart read ref after an await with no ref.mounted guard
why: Both onEnqueueDrain closures (in syncWriteFacadeProvider and outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider) do a ref.read after an await with no ref.mounted check, violating SM-4. Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException if ref is used after its provider has rebuilt. Both providers watch activeProfileIdProvider/authStateProvider, which change on every profile switch or sign-out -- realistic during the network round-trip a drain takes. If that happens between the two awaits, the second ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt() throws on a stale ref. The surrounding comment (sync_providers.dart:100-104) spells out the user-visible cost of skipping recordDrainAttempt: 'the badge stays at its old value (e.g. a stale Synced) ... a false-Synced when the push failed.' Because this closure runs inside unawaited(tee().catchError((Object _) {})) in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart, the resulting exception is silently swallowed (see the companion EH-3 finding), so this failure currently has zero observability.
recommendation: Check ref.mounted after the first await in both closures before the second ref.read call, per SM-4; extract the duplicated closure body into one shared helper to fix both sites at once.
acceptance_criteria: custom_lint/riverpod_lint rule flagging ref use after an await without a mounted check (SM-4 Enforce backstop).
Provider test that rebuilds/switches the active profile mid-drain and asserts no UnmountedRefException reaches the caller and recordDrainAttempt either completes or is safely skipped.

title: OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue swallows every drain-tee failure with no log and no AppLogger field in the class
why: OutboxSyncWriteFacade never declares an AppLogger field, so this catchError has no way to log even if it wanted to. Any exception from the drain tee -- including the UnmountedRefException from the companion SM-4 finding, or a genuine permission-denied/network failure -- is discarded with zero trace. Every push*/enqueue* method in this class, used for every sync write in the app, funnels through this one _enqueue, making it the single choke point where all fire-and-forget drain failures currently vanish silently. No test in this batch (including the 1184-line local_data_upload_service_test.dart, which never wires onEnqueueDrain) exercises this path either.

title: LocalDataUploadService.pushAllLocalData enqueues every entity kind via a per-row awaited loop instead of a batched outbox write

title: Log or type the catch blocks that silently swallow errors across CurriculumActivationService/AddTrackFlow/EditTrackScreen
rule: EH-3 (every catch rethrows, converts, or logs via AppLogger — no log-less catch)
why: curriculum_activation_service.dart's _syncToFirestore catches ANY exception from pushing a profile's tracks to Firestore and does nothing but a comment ('Silent fail for offline/auth issues') — if the push starts failing for a persistent, non-offline reason, that profile's track state never reaches Firestore again, forever, with zero log/telemetry trail, in a codebase whose git history shows repeated real cross-device sync bugs ('eliminate active_curricula split-brain', 'sync FK crash', 'restore profile-scoped tracks'). The two stagesConfig/schedule JSON-parse catches mask malformed seeded program/stage data the same silent way. The two `on TutorWriteException catch (e)` blocks only surface the 'permission-denied' code; any other TutorWriteException code is dropped with no log and no user feedback, so a tutor-mode write failure for any other reason looks like nothing happened.
recommendation: Add an AppLogger.instance.warning/error(...) call to each listed catch before continuing (even when the UI intentionally stays silent), and add an else/log branch for unhandled TutorWriteException codes.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 listed catch blocks logs the caught exception via AppLogger before returning/continuing
A test that throws a non-'permission-denied' TutorWriteException from the mocked service asserts a log call or a surfaced message

corrections: The two `on TutorWriteException catch (e)` sites are NOT log-less in the broader sense claimed: tutored_write_router.dart:351-354 logs 'tutored_write_router_cf_failure' via AppLogger before throwing, so there is a telemetry trail upstream. The finding's 'zero log/telemetry trail' framing applies fully only to curriculum_activation_service.dart:220; the other 5 sites are lower-stakes (missing user feedback / defensive-default masking, not silent-forever failures).

title: Replace hand-rolled ==/hashCode in TrackBlueprint's value objects with @freezed
rule: Naming/placement/invariants — never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes
why: coding-standards.md is explicit: hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping. AddTrackDraft's hand-rolled == (track_blueprint_draft_repository.dart:66-73) proves it: it omits scopeSelectionsJson and studyDays from both == and hashCode, so two drafts differing only in scope or study-days compare equal; its own test (track_blueprint_draft_repository_impl_test.dart:95-113) only exercises equality on navStepIndex/curriculumKey/programId and never asserts inequality on the omitted fields, so the gap is untested. track_blueprint.dart repeats the same hand-rolled pattern across 6 classes and add_track_result.dart's BulkMarkIntent makes 8 sites total, even though the codebase already has a working @freezed sealed-union convention elsewhere (goal_entity.dart, sync_status.dart, restore_status.dart). Two of the three files are currently dead code (see the migration-trio finding), which caps today's practical blast radius, but the pattern remains a trap for anyone who revives them or copies the style into new code.
recommendation: Convert TrackBlueprint's value objects and AddTrackDraft to @freezed sealed classes/records; add a test asserting inequality on the currently-omitted fields before/while converting.
acceptance_criteria: track_blueprint.dart and track_blueprint_draft_repository.dart's value types are @freezed with generated ==/hashCode
A test asserts two AddTrackDraft/TrackBlueprint instances differing only in a previously-omitted field are NOT equal

corrections: Stronger than claimed: TrackBlueprint's own ==/hashCode (track_blueprint.dart:314-333, evidence already cited) has the identical omission bug (drops studyDays AND scopeSelections), not just AddTrackDraft's — finding under-states rather than over-states its case.

title: Deduplicate TrackCreationService/TrackEditService's verbatim study-day persistence loop

why: _saveStudyDaysLocal (track_creation_service.dart:348-368) and _saveStudyDays (track_edit_service.dart:95-115) are byte-for-byte identical except a parameter name — the exact 'delete then loop-await-upsert' method copy-pasted into two sibling services. title: Wrap TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl's save/reset methods' two DAO writes in a single transaction (DB-2)
why: saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each perform two sequential, separately-awaited local Drift writes (upsertOrder/deleteByTrack, then trackDao.stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction() wrapper. If the process dies between the two statements (app kill, OS low-memory kill — routine on mobile), the reorder is saved but the 'reorder-amnesty' stamp is not, so the scheduler keeps showing items as overdue that the user just reordered past — the exact bug the stampReorderAt call exists to prevent (per the file's own '§10.1' comments). stage_definition_repository_impl.dart's reorderStages in the same batch already demonstrates the correct pattern (_stageDao.runTransaction(...)) for the identical class of problem.
recommendation: Wrap each pair of DAO calls in `_database.transaction(() async { ... })`, mirroring the pattern already used in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart.reorderStages.
acceptance_criteria: All three methods wrap both DAO calls in one _database.transaction() block.

title: Stop interpolating e.toString() directly into tutoring error/snackbar text
why: manage_grants_screen.dart and manage_tutors_screen.dart interpolate a raw Dart exception's toString() into an otherwise-localized ARB string 4 times, so a Hebrew UI sentence ends with an untranslated English/technical fragment (e.g. a gRPC status string). The 6 matching data-layer sites (firestore_tutor_grant_repository.dart x6, tutor_write_service.dart x1) manufacture that raw string in the first place by stuffing `e.toString()` into the Failure.message field instead of a stable code, which is exactly the custom_lint `no_e_to_string_in_ui` rule this repo already has defined (currently non-enforcing because custom_lint is broken repo-wide).
recommendation: In the 4 UI catch blocks, map to a generic localized fallback (as invite_tutor_screen.dart already does for TutorGrantFailure) instead of interpolating e.toString(); in the data layer, log e.toString() via AppLogger and return a stable failure code instead of stashing the raw text in the value the UI eventually reads.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'e.toString()' lib/features/tutoring/presentation/ returns no UI-text interpolation sites.
Widget test confirms a thrown exception during revoke/rescind/load shows a fixed localized string regardless of the exception's message.

corrections: The lint source (packages/custom_lints/lib/src/rules/no_e_to_string_in_ui.dart) scopes strictly to files under '/presentation/'. It would NOT catch the 7 data-layer sites (data/repositories, data/services) even if custom_lint worked — only the 4 UI sites are covered by that specific lint. The 'why' text's claim that data-layer sites are 'exactly' this lint is inaccurate; those sites are EH-5 violations only. Doesn't change validity/severity of the underlying finding.

title: Delete or wire up the dead TutorAuditLogWriter path (tutor_audit_log_writer.dart / audit_log_providers.dart)
why: A repo-wide grep confirms `TutorAuditLogWriter` is constructed nowhere in lib/ — its 228 lines and the `TutorAuditLogRepository` interface it depends on are unreachable. Its own provider (`tutorAuditLogWriteRepositoryProvider`) resolves to `_StubAuditLogWriteRepository`, a permanent no-op with an ID-less TODO. The class's doc-comment claims 'every tutor write path... calls through this writer' and that entryId format is 'timestamp + 10 random hex chars (26 chars total)', but the actual `_log()` implementation has no random suffix at all — two same-millisecond calls for the same action type would collide on entryId, and per the interface's own idempotency contract ('duplicate writes with the same ULID are silently ignored') the second entry would be silently dropped if this code were ever revived as-is. Cross-checked functions/src/index.ts: the real audit trail is written server-side by each tutor*CF via `writeAuditLog(...)`, so there is no current production gap — this is confusing, misdocumented dead weight, not a live data-loss bug.
recommendation: Delete TutorAuditLogWriter, TutorAuditLogRepository, and the stub/provider if the server-side CF audit writes are now the sole source of truth; if a client-side path is still intended, wire a real Firestore-backed implementation and fix the entryId generator to match its documented ULID claim, with a DNI-#### ticket on the TODO either way.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'TutorAuditLogWriter' lib/ returns nothing, or returns a live call site plus a non-stub repository.
No bare `TODO(...)` without a DNI-#### id remains in audit_log_providers.dart (AG-6 grep clean).
