title: Convert TutorPermissions to @freezed instead of hand-writing ==/hashCode
why: coding-standards.md is explicit: domain value objects must be `@freezed` with generated `==`/`hashCode`/`copyWith`, specifically because hand-rolled equality drifts from the field list. TutorPermissions — its own doc-comment calls it 'Immutable value object' / 'VO' — hand-writes both operators across 9 fields, plus a separately hand-written constructor, copyWith, toFirestore, and fromFirestore: 5 places a future field addition must be updated by hand. The drift risk is already visible today: `canMarkLiveCompletion` is deliberately excluded from both `==` and `hashCode` (harmless only because it is hardcoded false for every instance) — exactly the kind of silent omission @freezed generation would make structurally impossible.
recommendation: Convert TutorPermissions to a @freezed class (keeping canMarkLiveCompletion as a computed getter rather than a constructor field, or a private default so it can't be set), and delete the hand-written ==/hashCode/copyWith.
acceptance_criteria: TutorPermissions.freezed.dart is generated; no hand-written operator == or hashCode remains in tutor_permissions.dart.
Existing TutorPermissions unit tests (defaults/readOnly/toFirestore round-trip) still pass unmodified.

title: Handle mid-loop failure in TutoredWriteRouter.pushStageDefinitions (tutored_write_router.dart)
rule: Nygard (partial I/O failure) / DB-6 offline-first parity
why: pushStageDefinitions awaits one Cloud Function call per stage sequentially and _handleResult throws immediately on the first TutorWriteFailure. If a tutor edits several stages at once and the network drops partway through, the earlier stages are already committed server-side while the remaining ones are simply lost — the thrown TutorWriteException names only the failing stage, not which stages already succeeded. Unlike the normal (non-tutored) write path, tutored writes deliberately bypass the local outbox (per this file's own header comment), so there is no retry queue to pick the dropped stages back up on reconnect — the class's offline-first guarantee (DB-6, exercised everywhere else in this app) does not hold here. This is architectural/edge-case reasoning, not a reproduced runtime failure.
recommendation: Either batch the per-stage calls into a single CF invocation (atomic on the server) or collect per-stage results and surface a structured partial-failure summary (which stages succeeded/failed) so the caller can retry just the failed subset instead of losing silent state.
acceptance_criteria: A test that fails the 2nd of 3 stage upserts asserts the caller learns which stages succeeded (not just a single opaque exception).
Documented decision (in tutored_write_router.dart's header) on whether partial multi-stage failure is an accepted risk or gets a retry path.

recommendation: Extract each screen's per-step bodies (_buildReadyToAccept/_buildSuccess/_buildError etc., and the _GrantRow/_TutorGrantRow row widgets) into presentation/widgets/ files.
acceptance_criteria: find lib/features/tutoring -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' returns empty.

title: Guard int.parse(sel.profileId) in tutored_write_router.dart
rule: EH-3/EH-4 (unhandled exception type breaks the class's stated contract)
why: The class doc says 'CF failures... are re-thrown as TutorWriteException so callers can surface a clear snackbar,' but int.parse(sel.profileId) is called unguarded at 10 sites before any CF call happens. If profileId is ever non-numeric (malformed TutoredProfileSelection, future ID-scheme change), a raw uncaught FormatException propagates instead of the documented TutorWriteException — no AppLogger context, and callers that specifically catch TutorWriteException per this class's contract won't catch it. No test in s1_tutored_write_router_test.dart exercises a non-numeric profileId, so this is unconfirmed in practice.
recommendation: Parse once via a small helper (e.g. `_profileIdOrThrow(sel)`) that logs via AppLogger and throws a typed TutorWriteException on failure, matching the class's documented error contract; call it once instead of int.parse at each of the 10 sites.
acceptance_criteria: A test that constructs a TutoredProfileSelection with a non-numeric profileId and calls any pushX method asserts a TutorWriteException (not FormatException) is thrown and logged.

title: Add ref.mounted guards after awaits in manage_tutors_providers.dart's incomingTutorGrantsProvider
why: incomingTutorGrantsProvider watches `authStateProvider.select((s) => s.currentUser?.firebaseUid)` and then awaits two network/DB calls before touching `ref.read` three more times (lines 118, 124, 131). If the watched uid changes mid-flight (e.g. the tutor signs out while this fetch is in progress — the exact account-switch race this file's own comments say it must defend against), Riverpod 3 tears down this build invocation and a subsequent `ref.read` throws UnmountedRefException instead of the intended AsyncError/graceful outcome. No `ref.mounted` check guards any of the three post-await reads.
recommendation: Check `if (!ref.mounted) return const <TutorGrant>[];` (or equivalent) immediately after each await before touching ref again, mirroring the SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in Notifier methods.
acceptance_criteria: A test that invalidates authStateProvider's uid while incomingTutorGrantsProvider's future is pending does not throw UnmountedRefException.

corrections: The 'why' text's line list (118, 124, 131) is slightly off — 131 is an await, not a ref.read; the second post-await ref-touch is actually line 121 (ref: ref, passed to buildTutoredMirrorWipeService).

title: Catch and log exceptions around TutorPinService calls in the PIN entry/setup async handlers
why: _onPinComplete (gate) and _onConfirmPinEntered (setup) wrap their await in try/finally with no catch clause. TutorPinService.verifyTutorPin/setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException — an underlying secure-storage failure (a real class of Android keystore/PlatformException issue this environment has hit before per the App Check debug-token flakiness on wipes) propagates as a raw, uncaught exception. Because _onPinComplete is invoked fire-and-forget (not awaited) from _appendDigit, the failure is swallowed by whatever global handler exists, with zero AppLogger call from this site and zero user feedback: _isVerifying resets to false in the finally block but _errorMessage stays null and _digits stays at 4 filled dots, leaving the user staring at a stalled numpad with no explanation and no way to retype until they notice backspace still works.
recommendation: Add a typed catch around the await that logs via AppLogger and sets a generic, localized _errorMessage (consistent with EH-2's 'no raw exception reaches presentation').
acceptance_criteria: _onPinComplete and _onConfirmPinEntered both have a catch block that calls AppLogger.instance.error and sets a localized _errorMessage
a test that makes the stubbed TutorPinService throw confirms the screen shows an error state instead of a silent stall

corrections: Minor: 'setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException' overstates it — setTutorPin has zero exception handling (no lockout check exists for set), so it's worse than stated, not misleading in finder's favor.

title: Type and log the catch block in TutorPinResetScreen._sendResetEmail
why: The bare `catch (e)` has no `on X` type, so per Dart semantics it catches everything thrown — including Error subtypes (StateError, TypeError, NoSuchMethodError from a programmer bug) — and silently converts all of them into the same generic 'send failed' UI message with zero AppLogger call. A real programming defect elsewhere in the call chain would present identically to a normal network failure, with no trace to diagnose it.
recommendation: Catch a specific exception type (or at least log via AppLogger.instance.error before setting the UI message) so Error subtypes are not silently masked and failures are traceable.
acceptance_criteria: the catch block logs via AppLogger with the exception and stack trace before updating _errorMessage
the catch is narrowed to typed exceptions the send/clear operations can actually throw, not a bare catch(e)

title: Stop misreporting a failed local PIN clear as a failed reset email in TutorPinResetScreen
why: sendPasswordResetEmail and clearTutorPin are two sequential awaits inside one try block with one shared catch that always sets the l10n key tutorPinResetSendFailed ('Failed to send reset email...'). If the email send succeeds but the subsequent local-PIN-clear throws (a real possibility given documented secure-storage flakiness in this environment), the user is told the email failed when it actually sent — they will retry, triggering a second real password-reset email, while the actual failure (local PIN not cleared) goes unaddressed and unreported.
recommendation: Split the two operations into separate try/catch blocks (or at minimum track which step failed) so the error message and retry behavior match what actually happened.
acceptance_criteria: a failure in clearTutorPin after a successful sendPasswordResetEmail does not show the 'send failed' string
a regression test simulates clearTutorPin throwing after a successful email send and asserts the UI does not claim the email failed

title: Add a shared pumpApp test helper instead of hand-rolled MaterialApp boilerplate in tutoring widget tests

If the delegate list or a future global wrapper (e.g. a text-scale clamp) needs to change, every file must be edited individually instead of one helper, and any file that gets the delegate list slightly wrong silently diverges in l10n behavior from its siblings.
recommendation: Introduce test/helpers/pump_app.dart exposing a pumpApp(tester, child, {locale, overrides}) helper and migrate these call sites (and the wider suite) onto it.
acceptance_criteria: test/helpers/pump_app.dart exists with a single MaterialApp+delegates definition
the 4 files in this batch build their widget-under-test through the shared helper instead of inlining MaterialApp

title: Replace tautological isNotNull(Type)/constructor-tearoff compile-checks with real interface/constructor assertions

The docstrings explicitly claim these verify 'that FirestoreTutorGrantRepository satisfies the TutorGrantRepository interface' and that 'the class is constructible without error' — neither claim is actually checked: an accidental removal of `implements TutorGrantRepository`, or a constructor that throws on null functions, would leave these tests green.

title: Add semantics to PIN numpad icon-only controls and remove the fixed-height digit-key wrapper
why: The AppBar close IconButton and the numpad's backspace key are icon-only with no tooltip/Semantics label, so a screen-reader user cannot identify either control (the digit keys are fine — their Text child is auto-exposed). Separately, _TutorPinKey wraps its child (a 24sp digit Text at default scale) in a fixed SizedBox(height: 52); no global TextScaler clamp exists in this app (verified via grep), so at large accessibility text-scale settings the digit glyph can exceed the fixed box and clip or overflow visually.
recommendation: Add `tooltip:` to the close IconButton and wrap the backspace Icon in Semantics(label: ...) or give it a tooltip; remove the fixed height on _TutorPinKey (let it size to content with padding, or clamp textScale for the digit only).

title: Convert TutorPinResult switches in gate/setup screens from statements to switch expressions per EH-6
why: coding-standards.md EH-6 states closed variant sets must be modeled as sealed + 'switch over it with switch expressions; never add a default:/_ arm.' Both files use switch STATEMENTS (case Pattern: followed by statement blocks) over the sealed TutorPinResult, not the mandated expression form (contrast with tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart's `child: switch (_step) { ... => ..., }`, which does it correctly). Functionally harmless today — Dart's exhaustiveness checker covers statement-form switches too — but it's a textual violation of an explicitly documented, partially-enforced standard, and inconsistent with the sibling file in the same feature.
recommendation: Rewrite both switches as switch expressions (`TutorPinSuccess() => widget.onPinVerified(), ...`), matching tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart's style.
acceptance_criteria: both switches use the `Pattern => ...,` expression form with no default/_ arm
